💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests.
  • Sources indicate that if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode.
  • Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that you can have a ton of fun in GTA 6 even if you only follow the core gameplay loop of running around, stealing cars, and completing missions and side quests. However, if you take a minute to learn a few hidden controls, I think you'll enjoy the game even more. These are fairly simple controls that let you hide from the cops, trash talk other drivers, or flip the bird when you're feeling like annoying NPCs. These are 10 of the best hidden GTA 6 controls that'll help you unlock an entirely new side of the game.

Sources indicate that if you just want to sit back and relax as your character drives around Leonida in GTA 6, you should try the auto-drive mode. It's a relaxing way to enjoy the streets without having to worry about following traffic rules. To enable it, you need to get in a vehicle and add a waypoint on the map. This serves as your character's destination, so if you want a longer drive, be sure to drop the waypoint far, far away. Next, hold the down arrow on the D-Pad, and press the Option button. This enables cinematic mode. Then, hold the Circle button to enable auto-drive.

Your character is going to commit a lot of crimes in GTA 6. When this happens, you attract heat, and soon enough, cops will begin chasing you. Switching cars is a great way to reduce the amount of attention you get from law enforcement, but you can still be identified by your face or clothing. Until you can reach a safe spot to swap outfits, maintain a low profile by ducking while driving. Hold the Circle button while driving to duck.

In a recent development, EA's Road Rash was among the first racing games I played as a child, and I remember how much fun it was to kick your rivals while speeding through the game's various courses. You can have a taste of that in GTA 6 too. Press the Square button while you're riding a bike, and your character will kick anyone who's near you. If you do this in a car, it opens the door, and hits people around the car. To annoy other drivers, press R3, and your character will direct some trash talk towards NPCs.

Industry observers note that hold Circle to lean back against walls, or to sit on the beach. To rest on a ledge, you can hold L3. This lets you take a moment to soak in beautiful views in the game, or lounge around as you listen to NPC conversations. Paying attention to those conversations can lead to some fun side quests, and sometimes give you a tip or two for quick money or other rewards.

Industry observers note that if you really want to rile people up in GTA 6, you can flip the bird. This works only when your character is unarmed. Hold L2, focus on a person, then press R1. Actions have consequences in GTA 6, so be prepared to fight NPCs when you do this.

When you're being chased by cops, enemies, or angry NPCs, you can use a quick shortcut to look back without turning the camera around. Just hold R3 to look behind you.

According to recent reports, while driving, press Circle to toggle headlights (and switch to high beams). This is particularly useful when you're offroading at night. You can also hold left arrow on the D-Pad, and move the right stick up to access other vehicle controls like hazard lights, opening or closing windows, etc., in case you want to add to the realism.

In a recent development, stealing emergency vehicles in GTA 6 is risky, but the reward is totally worth it. Not only do you find stashes of weapons, gear, and money in some of these vehicles, but you also have access to sirens that help you clear traffic off your path. If you steal an ambulance or a cop car, hold L3, and move the left stick up to go through different siren tones. Press L3 and the left stick up to enable the siren.

GTA 6 is a third-person game, but it has a first-person mode that partially works. It is useful for looking at smaller objects around your character, such as posters, small signs, or to look for clues in and around a house. (Yes, I am talking about Mandy's creepy house and bad vibes.) Hold L2 + hit R3 to switch to first-person mode. Sadly, you can't move when you do this, but you can look around. Try it in Mandy's property to observe a few nasty surprises.

Sources indicate that when you sprint towards a car, press the X button to slide across the hood. This is much faster and smoother than running around parked cars or jumping over them. It also looks cool, which is reason enough to try this feature.

#154936. Tech Report: EA Sports FC 27 to resurrect John Motson with help from generative AI, because apparently football games need someone yelling about goals from beyond the grave

Tech Report: EA Sports FC 27 to resurrect John Motson with help from generative AI, because apparently football games need someone yelling about goals from beyond the grave

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (710 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In today's instance of a sentence I never thought I'd write, English football commentator John Motson has followed in the footsteps of Darth Vader.
  • Recent findings suggest that EA revealed Motson's resurrection for FC 27 to the BBC, with the deceased commentator's voice being made up of combination of old recording sessions and generative AI.
  • "My dad was the least technological person in the world," Motson's son Fred said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In today's instance of a sentence I never thought I'd write, English football commentator John Motson has followed in the footsteps of Darth Vader. In the latest instance of a game featuring a dead celebrity's voice reanimated with help from generative AI, EA Sports FC 27 will soon have Motson offering words about passes and shots that clank off the bar despite him having died in 2023.

Recent findings suggest that EA revealed Motson's resurrection for FC 27 to the BBC, with the deceased commentator's voice being made up of combination of old recording sessions and generative AI. The publishers got permission from Motson's widow and son to do this, and told the BBC they'd not have gone ahead if Motson's family - whom EA have paid an undisclosed sum for the rights to use Motson's likeness and recreate his voice - hadn't been on board.

"My dad was the least technological person in the world," Motson's son Fred said. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically - but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects.".

Recent findings suggest that EA senior game design director Mat Prior remarked AI has been used for the likes of lines in which Motson talks about modern players who don't feature in the old excerpts of him calling games. You'd think that might've been the point at which EA began to question why it's necessary to resurrect Motson for the purpose of commentating on games featuring a number of players he might never have watched while he was alive, meaning we don't know what unique calls he might have made in response to seeing them strut their stuff. Alas, it seems that wasn't the case.

According to recent reports, "From a gaming standpoint, it's something we've used for many years - like machine learning to help drive animation systems and so on and so forth," Prior added. "It's not there to replace commentators in any way shape or form...there's certainly no future prepares to replace anyone with AI." It's worth noting EA already use genAI to replicate the voices of some living commentators with their permission, with the justification given being that it helps cut down on the amount of work required to record hours of a real human saying different player names with different inflections.

Sources indicate that motson served as a commentator on FIFA 96 through 05, but looks to have been absent from the series since that point aside from briefly popping up for a return in FIFA 19. So, aside from that late 2010s one-off, Motson hadn't been part of one of EA's football games for about two decades prior to this AI-enabled resurrection for FC 27. I'd argue that makes it a lot more difficult to make the case for this use of genAI. It's not like the tech's being used to help maintain continuity with a voice that's always been part of the series' furniture, as is the case with Witcher 3 devs CD Projekt Red's modification of Geralt's Polish voice via genAI in the Songs of the Past DLC following actor Jacek Rozenek's stroke. In that case, the actor was also alive to give his direct permission.

Whether families or estates should be able to permit the use of AI cloning on the voices of actors or performers who didn't give written permission for it while they were alive is a matter of much contention. Actor Peter Caulfield, who's been arguing for greater protections against AI voice cloning through a campaign called Save Our Voices Now, argued in the BBC piece that it should only be allowed in cases where living people have signed deals to allow it.

Industry observers note that personally, I think games should probably do without genAI-fuelled celebrity ressurections, especially in scenarios where there seems no pressing need to do so. Even Tupac's likeness being used without any AI bollocks in RGG Studio's upcoming historical beat 'em up Stranger Than Heaven feels unsettling. AI Motson will be added to FC 27 as an optional commentator on November 26th.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that chicago Fire is now in its 15th season on the 2026 TV schedule, and this season the show has gone through some casting changes. Original cast member Joe Miñoso officially exited as Joe Cruz in the 300th episode, but he wasn’t the only one to do so. After just a couple of seasons, Dermot Mulroney mentioned goodbye to Firehouse 51, departing as Battalion Chief Dom Pascal in the Season 15 premiere. He was solid in the role, however, and I wanted to know if he’d ever come back.

In a recent development, mulroney joined Chicago Fire in the Season 13 premiere as 51’s newest Chief, replacing Eamonn Walker’s Wallace Boden. While things started off a bit rocky with the crew, Pascal grew on 51 and 51 on Pascal. In Season 14, it's worth noting Mulroney was absent for a chunk of episodes, but he returned at the very end. Unfortunately, his return didn’t stick, because he left for good at the beginning of Season 15.

Even though we just said goodbye to him, fresh showrunner Victor Teran told CinemaBlend about the possibility of Pascal popping up at 51 again. He told me "anything's possible" and elaborated on that, telling CinemaBlend the connection with Severide could indicate more down the line.

According to recent reports, I think we are always on the lookout for interesting storylines for our characters who've left the show. So we'll definitely stay on the lookout for a place. I think because of the way he mentored and guided Severide into this chair and really allowed it to happen in some ways. He'll always remain a critical part of that. And so I think it's very possible that he could emerge down the road, but he's also got a career in Phoenix for himself that he's off to.

Unlike a lot of characters on TV who get killed off, Chicago Fire included, Pascal's story was left open. He left 51 in Kelly’s hands and, as Teran pointed out, is now building his career in Arizona. That said, he became close with the firehouse and obviously made a mark in a short amount of time, and made sure that Kelly was ready to take over. I would love nothing more than to see Pascal again, and I could not be happier to hear Teran's response. Since Mulroney was not happy about the exit, he probably wouldn't be opposed to coming back.

Despite Chicago Fire’s revolving door of stars, the series has brought back a handful of former cast members from time to time. Since the show doesn’t seem to have any end in sight, it’s entirely possible that we’ll be seeing Pascal again, and not just because of what Teran told me. Chicago Fire always seems to bring back characters when you least expect it, so you never know what could happen. They just need to find a reason for him to be back in the Windy City.

Meanwhile, Chicago Fire has been turning up the heat in Season 15. There are a handful of newbies who joined Fire as firefighter candidates. Even though it’s been fun to see Stella in more of a leadership role, it’s also been hard. One newbie got some bad news and was let go from the CFD, and I’m worried it could bring some consequences for Stella and Kelly. It's been exciting beyond characters just leaving the show.

Right now, Chicago Fire is on a brief hiatus for Thanksgiving, but the series will be back on December 9 for the fall finale, and there will certainly be some action to watch out for that Wednesday. In the meantime, all episodes are streaming with a Peacock subscription.

According to recent reports, it’s the first Chinese esports title to reach DreamHack, featuring teams that have been selected through a full professional league system. Six regions offered a route to the offline finals, and the twelve squads competing this weekend are as follows:.

Sources indicate that fnatic are, of course, well known to DreamHack audiences, having won the first League of Legends World Championship there back in 2011, as well as the first CS:GO Major in 2013. Alliance, being a Swedish team, will be playing on home soil, but only time will tell if this gives them an additional boost. They, and the ten other teams to have gone the distance, will once again be competing for a share of a $500,000 prize pool.

In a recent development, one core aspect of Delta Force that’s attracted upcoming fans over the last twelve months is its commitment to extraction as an esport. Whereas in traditional FPS competitions there’s an obvious focus on winning fights, in Delta Force’s Operations mode, information gathering, firefights, resource management and extraction decisions all play out within a single match.

With three days of intense competition on the horizon, its future certainly looks bright.

Delta Force is free to play and available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Android, iOS, Google Play, Epic Games Store, and Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've lost count of how many times I've settled down to play a brand-latest game on Steam, only to be smacked in the face with a giant popup telling me to "Grab a controller and kick back!" instead of using my humble mouse and keyboard.

According to recent reports, thankfully for me I live in a multi-platform household, meaning a controller is never far out of reach. But I've also got staunch PC pals without a pad to pick up and who, rightly enough, don't want to fork out the kinda cash that PlayStation's DualSense or the Xbox controller require.

But I'm a firm believer that a good controller is a must-have tool in a PC gamer's repertoire these days, and we needn't immediately seek out the big names when it comes to a comfortable, robust gamepad. Tons of budget-friendly options have popped up on the market over the years, and while some of them are admittedly pretty naff there are also a bunch of great controllers that won't break the bank.

According to recent reports, in fact, I've got three of 'em for under $25 for you right here. That's a third of the price of a DualSense controller! While they don't come with fancy haptics and adaptive triggers, they do offer stick-drift resistant, low-latency gaming. Which, as fun as the bells as whistles can be, are really the most crucial bits.

A fresh and improved version of the original Nova Lite, the Nova Lite 2 has Hall effect everything, 1000 Hz polling, and trigger locks. It even has a mechanical D-pad, which is absurd for the money, really.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect.

Price check: Amazon $29.99 (Grey).

Out of the three choices, our pad professional James Bentley tells me he likes the GameSir Nova Lite 2 the best, currently going for $23 at Walmart. It boasts comfort, decent polling, and Hall effect—so much better protection against that pesky stick drift. It's also got our highest review score out of the bunch thanks to its affordability, mechanical d-pad, and choice of 2.4Ghz and Bluetooth.

Sources indicate that it's not got great grip, however, and its budget is felt in the less-than-stellar plastic and rather simple software. But for the price you're paying? It's a great, basic choice for those who only need to reach for a controller occasionally.

According to recent reports, we've already raved about Hall effect joysticks and how they spell the end for the dreaded stick drift. In this wireless gaming controller, they're a welcome feature, but this handful of gaming hardware packs a few quirky surprises too. For instance, there are extra bumper buttons.

Key specs: Hall effect sticks, triggers | 2.4G wireless | 19 h battery.

Price check: Best Buy $21.99 (Black) | Walmart $29.99 (Purple).

But if you're someone who's accustomed to the likes of the Switch Pro controller, you might find the 8BitDo Ultimate 2C a better fit, right now going for $20 at Amazon. It's got a pretty similar shape, and also sports those beloved Hall effect joysticks. It does have a little bit of a mushy d-pad but hey, look at that lovely colourway!

According to recent reports, finally, if you're looking to spend as little as possible, the GameSir Nova Lite comes in as the cheapest option at a mere $18. It's got less mappable buttons than its successor thanks to no back paddles, and is overall a downgrade. For the extra four bucks I'd personally just go for the newer version, but if you're really looking to really squeeze every cent, it's certainly an option worth considering.

It's incredible to think you can spend so little and get a stick drift-resistant wireless controller that doesn't completely suck. Luckily for the GameSir Nova Lite, it does all of the above and manages to feel good and light in the hands, too.

Key specs: Wireless (Bluetooth and 2.4 GHz) | Asymmetric | Hall effect.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar just issued a new patch for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, targeting a few issues players have been reporting since the game debuted last Thursday (19th November).

The 23rd November patch for the game deploys seven major fixes for the game, including a pretty significant bug that prevented phone calls not triggering at certain points, resulting in a scenario where you could be locked out of progressing the game. The official patch is titled 'version 01.002.002', and its weighs in at different sizes on different consoles: it's 603.8 MB on PS5, and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X/S.

Thanks to an patch on the Rockstar website, you can read all of the updates that arrive with the latest pathc below.

There have been a few fairly high-profile cases of the autosave not working as the developer intended, leading to a few cases of streamers losing plenty of real-world time thanks to unpredictable auto-save behaviour. JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress on the PS5, for example.

But there's one issue here the developer hasn't addressed: vignetting. Plenty of players have taken to online communities to complain about the vignette effect that pops into the game - theoretically to help with motion smoothing and various grapihcal elements as the game runs in 30FPS. THe effect is worsened when you're fatigued, hungry, or have some other status effect, but it is present quite a lot of the time, too. Most of the responses to a tweet about the patch posted by the Rockstar Support account reference the vignetting in GTA 6, and the developer has issued no response at the time of writing.

I am not the Ironclad, nor was meant to be; am an attendant lord, one that will do to bind a necro, Exhaust a scene or two, advise the Regent; no doubt, an easy tool, Defective, glad to be of use, Politic, Silent, and Impervious; full of high synergy, but a bit obtuse; at times, indeed, almost ridiculous— almost, at times, the Fool.

It has been a while since I played Slay the Spire 2. I return to find the forums full of grief concerning a recently introduced sixth character - a minstrel of sorts, dressed in carpets, who shoots arrows out of a harp.

The short version is that the Fool was wildly overpowered when Mega Crit added her to the early access deckbuilder's beta branch, with a base arrow-shooting mechanic that lets her dish out at least 21 damage in her first turn, and a Repeat Shot card that allows for upwards of 80. She ain't so vicious anymore, because they've just released a "mostly Fool-centric" patch that nerfs a couple dozen or so cards.

Recent findings suggest that it's not all nerfs – they've buffed Cho Chorus, Quietus and Show Off, among others, while reworking Tune, Flourescence and Rapid Shot. There's a newly introduced Rare card, Optimism, which exhausts all Sadness in your Hand, while drawing a card for every card exhausted.

Sources indicate that some context: Sadness is a special colourless card, earned by way of cards like Mourning Blow. It remains in your hand between turns and can't be played, making it an immediate hindrance, but you can transform it and use it as fuel for certain cards. Just like real sadness! Best of all, you can turn it into Joy, which grants you Energy. Reading about this complex neurophysical alchemy is making me tired. Shall I give the beta build a go? Do I dare to eat a peach? Are you sick of ham-fisted Prufrock references yet?

Read the full patch notes here. The Fool is an interesting creation, eyebrow-raising damage output aside, and I look forward to her addition to the game's main Steam branch. She can play various flavours of music to modify other cards.

Recent findings suggest that I do like a weird bard, and I broadly approve of the practice of releasing fresh early access characters with all the sliders pushed to max, waiting for the cacophonous whining to reach a certain pitch, and then jocularly chopping back their stats. I should get back into Slay the Spire 2. I just have to play [redacted] first.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a new trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

According to recent reports, the trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and fresh playable faction.

In a recent development, now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was revealed, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

In its final few seconds, the trailer indicates a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was quickly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively upcoming addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

It has been revealed that vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

What this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grabbing a Truffade Thrax in GTA 6 isn't too hard, but if you want Andrew Node's supercharged version, the true fastest car around, you'll need to complete a little collectible hunt. Before you start, it's worth noting that this special Truffade Thrax costs 70k to register when you steal it, though you can also sell it to Randy for 20k (not that I would recommend this as it's a unique car).

The first step is scanning ten No Flusher toilet graffiti stamps around Vice Beach, the east portion of Vice City, with your WAiNK It app. Each symbol is basically a little blue toilet. After that, you'll have to head to a secret lockup, and then you're on for stealing the car.

This first one is southeast of Nola - Ocean beach on the pavement on the west side of the road.

The second is east of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, on the south side pavement of the road leading out onto the grass towards the beach.

Industry observers note that this one is at the east end of the bridge leading from Vice Beach to Waxman Island, on the southern pavement. Also to the west of LTD Gas - Ocean Beach.

This fourth one is east of Aural Expert and north of Venus Fitness, on the pavement at the side of the junction.

This one is on the pavement directly in front of Banana Hole Main Bar, east down the road from the previous one above.

This sixth one is on the sidewalk on the far west of the road running along the bottom of the huge park in Vice Beach.

This seventh is west of Podium Sports - Ocean Beach, down the road you can see with the roundabout at the end on the map.

The eighth is east down the road from Shorefront - Ocean Beach bank and south of Easy Electronics, on the pavement on the corner.

This ninth is north of Marshal's jewelry and northeast of Endzone - Washington Beach, at the east end of the big carpark bordering the beach.

On the right side of the northern road at the Oldby Island junction, directly opposite Ron Gas - Washington Beach.

After you've found all ten, Cal's conspiracy theory chat (which unlocks after the first) will go dark, before you get a separate message a little later giving you their hideout location. Head there, read the note to the right of the garage door, and then look on the back of it to get the code for the lock:.

Inside you'll have a bunch of evidence pointing to Andrew Node's house on Starfish island, so examine it all and then you're ready to steal the car.

First off, Starfish Island is a gated community with security, so it's better to get a boat there. Head west from the hideout and steal a boat on the piers, then drive west across the water to the jetty of Andrew Node's house—it's the one on the southern side towards the centre, that looks like a backwards L.

Dock, head around the left side of the house to find a white garage on the right you can open up with Andrew Node's Truffade Thrax inside. You'll have to drive it off the island, but after that you can head to Randy and register it for 70k. Just make sure you have the garage space and the money before you steal the car.

Publisher Nintendo and developer Monolith Soft have released a three-minute overview trailer for Xenoblade Chronicles 3 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, which is due out on December 3.

Here is an overview of the game, via Nintendo:.

Industry observers note that in Xenoblade Chronicles 3 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, you will join Noah and Mio, members of the opposing nations of Keves and Agnus, as they embark on a stirring journey through a war-torn world that harbors a dark secret. Master real-time RPG combat and enjoy newly voiced event scenes, enhanced 4K resolution in TV mode (with compatible television), full HD in handheld mode, and smoother, sharper gameplay at 60 frames per second.

On this adventure, you’ll command six characters, as well as a new mythical Hero called Shimmer—a speedy attacker who unleashes devastating rapid-fire combos and wields the power of Foresight to see the future. Lead your band against hordes of enemies, auto-attacking with each character’s distinct Arts and weapons. Pairs of characters can also Interlink to form a mighty Ouroboros capable of taking down the most threatening enemies with powerful Arts.

In a recent development, you can also test your strength against waves of enemies in the new Heroes’ Vault mode. Here, with each enemy you defeat, you’ll power up a gauge you can use to enhance your abilities and gain additional allies. But choose wisely—you’ll need to prepare well to defeat the almighty foe awaiting you at the end of each mission!

Breaking: Paradox grand strategy Afterworld has a wasteland band mechanic that sounds worryingly like a continent-sized game of The Sims

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (907 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that much like a huge dust cloud gradually resolving into an army of skull-painted bikers, Paradox's post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld continues to take shape in the course of developer blog posts.
  • Sources indicate that each band has needs, satiation of which makes them feel more motivated and thus, more willing to follow your orders and work for the good of the tribe as a whole.
  • It appears to make for some alarming diversity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that much like a huge dust cloud gradually resolving into an army of skull-painted bikers, Paradox's post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld continues to take shape in the course of developer blog posts. The latest Parablog digs into what I think is one of the game's most interesting aspects – you don't control one single unified civ. Instead, you amass a motley tribe by befriending, conquering, or otherwise assimilating a range of individual wasteland bands.

Sources indicate that each band has needs, satiation of which makes them feel more motivated and thus, more willing to follow your orders and work for the good of the tribe as a whole. Some of the needs are more generic – for example, shelter, nutrition, hydration, medicine, social standing, and security against threats. Others are bespoke, shaped by Custom - another in-game social metric - and by that band's origins.

It appears to make for some alarming diversity. For example, you could have a band that are full vegetarian, and excel at foraging - they won't even eat dried insects, the hippies! You could also have a band of cannibals who have a literal Human Flesh consumption gauge. I see nothing in the latest dev diary to forbid you from assimilating both the cannibals and the vegetarians. Let's, er, not seat them next to each other at the next council meeting, unless we're really running low on finger food.

"All needs can scale by band size, level or other game state elements that make sense," the developers write. "Another thing to keep in mind is that different bands will value different needs depending on who they are or recent events. For example a band that’s experienced extreme hunger will get more motivation from nutrition, while a band on the council will expect to get more standing because of where they are in society, not just because of who they are.

"When all of these things come together, you are invited to pick which bands are important for your tribe’s goals," the blog continues. "Those bands are the ones you will pay the most attention to motivate. When you look more closely at what those bands actually want you will find narratively and systemically immersive choices to make. At one point a band may care about food because you are facing a famine, but then rumors of some dustland horror beyond the tribe borders scares everyone into caring more about security and downplaying their previous preoccupation with food.".

Industry observers note that the most "work-in-progress" part of Afterworld's band motivation system is managing the potential gulf between an individual band's needs and overall tribe policy. You can, for example, put troops in settlements to make bands feel "dominated", which "increases their motivation, bypassing the needs, and allows you to run parts of your tribe with the stick, while others get the carrot.".

The developers are "still iterating on this side of the system, but the intent is for such tactics to [offer] various degrees of sustainability for your tribe, depending on your set up and who your bands are". If you try to coerce a band, you run the risk of them blowing up in rebellion as and when the stick is removed. "This can result in cool moments like you taking down a bigger threatening tribe who’s keeping their lower classes under control through forced medical sedation, but it all comes apart when you find a way to sabotage or raid the source of the sedatives," the blog explains. Seems very fiendish! There are many points of comparison here with other Paradox games, of course. Before writing this piece, I asked Mark for his take on Afterworld based on many hours desecrating the Catholic Church and/or wine trade in Crusader Kings 3. He observed that the game sounds a bit like playing the unlanded leader of some adventurers in CK3. Myself, I wish I could make some precise references to the Europa Universalis series, but our resident expert Brendy (RPS in peace) left many moons ago to found some appalling indepedendent website or other. So I'm going to swing for the fences and say this feels like a continent-scale game of The Sims, except with groups of irradiated and tattooed, neo-Bronze age pillagers instead of smooth-faced burbanites. For the most informed appraisal of all, here's Julian's chat with Paradox about the game's procedural history generation - it writes you a latest apocalypse for every playthrough.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that ariana Grande is a wildly popular pop star and Oscar-nominated actress who has spent much of her life in the public eye. Over the past few years there's been a ton of discourse about her relationship with Cynthia Erivo while promoting the Wicked movies, as well as discourse about her appearance. The chatter got so loud that Grande took a step away from the public, although she recently reunited with Bowen Yang and talked about the backlash to her "Petal" music video.

According to recent reports, over the years Ariana Grande has spoken about her complicated relationship with the public, including discourse about her appearance and acting abilities. Those topics were addressed in her music video for "Petal", and during a recent appearance on the podcast Las Culturistas (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) the accomplished multihyphenate spoke about the story she was telling in that video, offering:.

It has been revealed that that was largely what the video was about is like 'Oh, here comes this little girl, talented little girl.' And there's always some distortion around the performance or around the art, whatever it is. And for a while she tries to... and then my favorite part is that she comes back to herself at the end. She's wearing the same color, she's wearing the same hair, she's wearing the same thing. And that's when they say they say to her 'It's just so weird, go back to your old you.' And she's like 'But I am! I've connected with my inner me. This is me trying again as me.'.

Industry observers note that grande addressed the "distortion" between her self-image and fan discourse throughout the entire album Petal, especially the title track. Clearly the 33 year-old singer saw the comments online, and backlash related to a change in her sound, the years-long Wicked promotional tour, as well as her personal appearance. Unfortunately, the "Petal" video inspired a new round of discourse that seemingly informed her decision to take some time away.

Shortly after the "Petal" video arrived online months ago, critics started commenting about her appearance, specifically her weight. This discourse started during Wicked, and continued despite Grande trying to address the chatter through her art. As she went on to share with Las Culturistas hosts Bowen Yang and Matt Rogers:.

Industry observers note that then that video with the intention of really spelling it out had its own meta insane perception that was just really interesting. But I feel so proud and grateful. I wouldn't change a thing. I would put it out today exactly as is. I wouldn't change a thing. I think my experience of putting art out and having people receive it is so different than how it used to be, even just a few years ago.

Fame is a double edged sword, and most of us would likely crack under the pressure of this backlash. Ariana Grande set some boundaries to care for her mental health, but she also seemingly stands by her artistic choices related to the "Petal" music video. She went on to explain her perspective about the outside voices, saying:.

Recent findings suggest that and now I really do feel as long as I'm creating from an authentic place, and being honest, and sharing what I know needs to come out and making things that I love I know. Let the chips fall where they may. My people will be my people. And it's okay if they're not.

That certainly sounds like a healthy way to approach any potential backlash that Ariana Grande faces moving forward. She's once again putting herself out there with her starring role in Focker In-Law, as well as the recently announced documentary The Eternal Sunshine Diaries (the latter of which is arriving for those with a Paramount+ subscription). Hopefully expressing herself honestly in both that doc and podcast appearances like Las Cultch can help quiet the chatter from naysayers who are constantly weighing in about her career, personal life, and appearance.

Focker In-Law is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list, while the two-part The Eternal Sunshine doc will arrive on Paramount+ December 11th and 12th.

  • Industry observers note that amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

In a recent development, variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first indicated up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Industry observers note that amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

Earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

In a recent development, there's no release date yet for the show, but it's remarked to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

Industry observers note that "We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica said at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon.".

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back, too.

"Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad.".

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It has been revealed that there are loads of Black Friday gaming headset deals at Currys, with the best reducing models down to lovely tempting prices.
  • This wired Logitech gaming headset is over 50% off, despite its specs.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you want your Nintendo Switch 2 to sound as good as possible, you won't dream of using the handheld's built-in stereo speakers, and will pick up a headset to use with the system. It won't cost you much to do so, with Black Friday deals cutting cost on gaming-designed headphones.

It has been revealed that there are loads of Black Friday gaming headset deals at Currys, with the best reducing models down to lovely tempting prices. Some are discounted to below £50, which means they're cheaper than the cost of a Switch 2 game. They're all wired models, as cable-toting tech is generally cheaper, which means these options still offer some impressive specs despite the low price. In particular there are four headsets below this price threshold which work on the Switch 2, and you can find them below, ordered from cheapest to priciest.

This wired Logitech gaming headset is over 50% off, despite its specs. It offers 7.1 sound, and is certified as a DTS Headphone:X headphone. It's pretty simple in terms of features, but it's a simple way of getting wired audio from your Switch (or any other console).

This gaming headset is roughly a year old, so is starting to see discounts. It gives you an affordable way to experience some of Turtle Beach's popular audio features, and it's pretty lightweight compared to rivals too.

HyperX offers a fair few gaming headsets we recommend, but thanks to the discount, this is perhaps the cheapest. It's surprisingly cheap when you consider it has dual drivers, offering sonic nuance many alternatives miss.

Industry observers note that coming just under the £50 threshold is this alternative HyperX model, which has a wider range of connection options than the above model and has a more durable frame. It's also designed to be comfortable with soft leatherette padding and memory foam cushions.

The main appeal of almost any gaming headset is thus: dedicated cans will sound better than the tinny loudspeakers you get in a handheld console. The presence of a proper microphone is a benefit too, if you play online with people.

If you usually play your Switch 2 on your home TV, while it's docked, you might not therefore need a gaming headset. Maybe your TV's built-in speakers, or the loudspeakers or soundbar you use for it, work just as well.

I'd therefore recommend a headset mostly to people who play their Switch 2 on the go. In many situations, you can't play your Switch out loud in the first place, so a headset is important, especially since all cans block out surrounding noise by virtue of their padded ear cushions.

But what about cheap versus expensive headsets? Honestly, I think pricey cans are best suited to competitive esports players who need to hear everything around them, or PC gamers who'll have much better access to the headphone software. Usually, what you're paying for is an elite roster of tools, features and preset EQ modes, and it's often hard to play around with those tools if you're not on a computer.

So for most buyers, a budget pair of cans like this is perfect, because audio quality is often the one thing you're not compromising on. The only thing you might want, that costs more, is a wireless connection. If you don't like the idea of using a physical cable, maybe you should pay a little bit more, but convenience is the only benefit to a Bluetooth connection in gaming headsets.

We've found all of the Black Friday retro deals you might want to spend money on, and you can also find Black Friday toy deals to tempt you.

#154921. Manufacturer of Heroes 3: Operation Torch review - moments of barely held-together chaos squandered by mechanical scripting

Manufacturer of Heroes 3: Operation Torch review - moments of barely held-together chaos squandered by mechanical scripting

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After waiting three years for Relic to expand Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, watching DLC after DLC focused on expanding the roster of units available in multiplayer matches, Operation Torch looks like a welcome addition.
  • Recent findings suggest that having played through the whole thing, I really want to say it's been worth the wait.
  • About halfway through the campaign, I'm put in charge of managing a retreat under a German advance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After waiting three years for Relic to expand Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, watching DLC after DLC focused on expanding the roster of units available in multiplayer matches, Operation Torch looks like a welcome addition. It's a newly introduced 15-mission campaign set in North Africa. following two US officers as they try to break the German Afrika Korps' hold on the region.

Recent findings suggest that having played through the whole thing, I really want to say it's been worth the wait. Unfortunately, it's not so straightforward as that.

About halfway through the campaign, I'm put in charge of managing a retreat under a German advance. While I must use my limited forces to hold back enemy troops at the head of the map, I'm also to drive a supply truck to different structures on the map so its crew can evacuate the buildings. It's a fraught start to the mission, forcing me to balance my attentions on the embattled front while also keeping a watchful eye on the vulnerable supply truck. German forces are seeping past the line and it would only take one well-placed anti-tank gun to spell an end to the evacuation.

The tension that comes in those moments, where I'm hopping about the battlefield barely holding things together, is Manufacturer of Heroes at its best. Operation Torch has several moments that reach that height of trying to command chaos, but they're squandered just as quickly as they come.

Recent findings suggest that when the three structures are broken down, I'm ordered to pull back to a hill outside of town. The mission isn't over, though: German officers are sifting through the abandoned buildings, looking for intel that was missed in the evacuation, and I'm to take two squads of snipers into enemy territory to kill them before they find anything. While it sounds exciting on paper, the mechanics of the mission's scripting make the reality underwhelming. My weakened army is sitting on a hill outside of town but no Germans come their way. In town, German units either stand still or travel in small looping patrols. Navigating the camouflaged sniper squads between them is easy work, but slow going. And even when they come out of stealth to shoot the officers and are spotted by a unit of German soldiers, they walk away from the fight and the Germans don't give chase. This may all be because I'm playing on standard difficulty, but the AI is oddly passive throughout Operation Torch.

Across multiple missions, I repeatedly used the same cheesing tactic. I would send a unit with the stealth passive to hide invisibly behind cover near the enemy, with strict orders not to open fire. With my infiltrator acting as a forward spotter, I'd then pummel the enemy with mortars from a safe distance. This tactic worked again and again. I knew, really, that it was no fun to do – turning every battle into a slow grinding down of the enemy – but it was also too effective to ignore when the enemy would never fight back.

Sources indicate that it's a shame so many of Operation Torch's missions hit a bum, overly-scripted note because I really enjoyed their unfurling narrative. Admittedly, my military history is poor, and all my knowledge of the North Africa campaign is drawn from the bits in SAS Rogue Heroes before they go to Europe, but my general understanding is that it was a campaign that saw rapid advances turn into just-as-quick retreats. This plays into Operation Torch's missions where success often isn't pushing the front forwards, but holding the line while covering routed allied forces, or defending a pass long enough for air support to arrive and cause enough damage to force the Germans to slow down. And, because you're battling backwards and forwards over the same territory, Relic employ one of my favourite RTS tricks: throwing you back into the same map but from a different perspective. In one mission you may be on the assault, prizing free the Afrika Korps' grip on a town street by street, but then a few missions later you find yourself defending the same territory from a retaliatory attack. It's unfortunate that the same push and pull isn't as evident on the battlefield.

Recent findings suggest that relic are experimenters, often reinventing a game's systems between entries in a series or trying out a latest mechanic in their expansions. In Operation Torch, the new toy is a choice of unlocks at the end of each mission. After a tank-focused assignment, for instance, you're offered a choice between a passive perk that makes Shermans 25% harder to hit while moving, or another which unlocks a different Sherman variant in your motor pool. Complete the map's optional objective and you also get to choose between a 10% reduction in tank costs and an upgrade that sees all your tanks produced at level 3 veterancy. These perks then apply throughout your campaign. By the final mission, the right side of your screen is a fat stack of passive and active perks. It's a neat idea but, in practice, it didn't seem to make a dramatic difference to how I played. I do like the idea of gradually developing your forces capabilities over a campaign but perhaps the difference needs to be more dramatic. Making your tanks slightly cheaper or harder to hit doesn't make that much of a tangible difference when you're right in there amidst the tracks and trenches.

In a recent development, thus, it really does fall back to the strength of Operation Torch's missions, which are sometimes great but too often a case of rolling over the enemy very, very slowly. Perhaps this is a game best played with the difficulty whacked up high.

While I was hoping for more from Operation Torch, mind, I do hope it's not the last time we see Relic flesh out Firm of Heroes 3's singleplayer. There's still plenty of scope there, and plenty of room for further experiments.

  • In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Banjo-Kazooie - the iconic Rare platformer starring an absent-minded bear and the sassy red bird he carries in a backpack - has been on hiatus for years, but a upcoming Activision job listing has raised hopes for a new game.

In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie.".

"Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on. "As a Product Manager, you will serve as the publishing product lead for an upcoming premium console & PC title, driving the product from concept to launch.".

It has been revealed that if you're scratching your brain trying to remember when Activision took control of the beloved platformer, well, it happened during Xbox's last massive internal shakeup. Amid the mass layoffs and studio divestments, Xbox also made some drastic changes to its corporate structure - Halo, World's Edge and Rare were all slotted under Activision's supervision.

Rare's 40-year history includes almost too many notable games to list, but the internal rejig presumably put Activision in control of games like Conker, Viva Pinata and Killer Instinct, alongside the aforementioned pirate hit Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie.

The job post is by no means confirmation that a newly introduced Banjo-Kazooie game is in development, but it is the only series named here that can be considered dormant, perhaps hinting that Activision has plans to revive it down the line. Crash Bandicoot 4 and Spyro: A Realm Beyond lay out a pretty good blueprint for its return, I think.

The last properly upcoming game in the series came 18 years ago with the Xbox 360's Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts, a surprisingly good physics-driven vehicle construction sandbox.

In a recent development, since then, Banjo and Kazooie demonstrated up as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros Ultimate. More recently, a fan-made PC port and an Evercade Double Pack have kept the series chugging.

Industry observers note that composer Grant Kirkhope was slightly more hopeful about the prospect of a Banjo-Threeie back in September. "I do know of like three companies that have actually physically pitched to Microsoft or to Rare about making another Banjo-Kazooie game, and I don't think anyone was successful," he noted at the time.

GTA 6 has been breaking records all over the place, so it doesn't come as much of a surprise to learn that its performance at physical retail has been mighty impressive.

Sources indicate that as reported by The Game Business, based on data from UK tracker Nielsen IQ, GTA 6 has recorded the country's largest physical launch since 2019's FIFA 20. Turns out only the nation's love of football can compete.

Recent findings suggest that GTA 6's physical sales generated £32 million in revenue in its first three days. Apparently, it's the 17th biggest physical launch in the UK ever.

All this has transpired despite the game's physical copies coming with a download code rather than a disc, something that caused some anguish among collectors and enthusiasts.

I think it maybe proves that people will still show up for a physical product, even in a world where discs are on their way out.

PlayStation aims to discontinue making discs for its platform starting in 2028, but it's possible we'll still see physical launches for major games — just with a code in the box instead of a Blu-ray.

Anyway, GTA 6 has been selling well on all fronts, surprise surprise. Did you pick up the physical version of the game? Tell us in the comments section below.

Industry News: AI May Be Scanning Your Private Signal Chats

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (416 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, if you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads.
  • It has been revealed that in a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy.
  • Signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you use Signal, it's likely you care at least a little bit about keeping your communication private so only you and those you're chatting with can see your message threads. Signal's end-to-end encryption keeps prying eyes out, but if you use agentic AI on your device, your chats may not be as locked down as you think.

It has been revealed that in a recent blog post, Signal president Meredith Whitaker outlined the potential threat AI assistants like Siri and Gemini pose to the platform's promise of privacy. Systems-level capabilities like Gemini Intelligence (on Android) and Siri AI's Onscreen Awareness (on iOS and macOS) scan your screen and may be able to capture data from Signal conversations in the process, which can then be used to perform tasks. Not only does this potentially expose your information, but that of other conversation participants as well. Whitaker notes that this leaves privacy protections outside of Signal's control because the platform cannot easily restrict AI access to the app.

Signal has already blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI, which by default was able to take and store screen grabs of Signal messages on Windows 11. While Signal cannot guarantee that AI won't have access to your data, there are a few protections now available for those on iOS and Android as well.

The main workaround in Signal for now is to restrict screenshots and screen recordings inside the app, though this does not prevent AI agents from potentially grabbing content from other parts of your device. According to Signal's support documents, these protections will now be enabled by default on iOS 27 and Android with the latest versions of the Signal app.

Users on iOS 27 can confirm or manually disable screenshot protection via Settings > Privacy > Block Siri AI. The compromise with this setting is that it also blocks you from taking screenshots of Signal conversations in the app and App Switcher, though you can disable it temporarily for 10 minutes if needed. On Android, Signal automatically engages the "Screen security" setting when it detects an AI agent attempting to access the screen. This, too, blocks screenshots inside the app and can be disabled via Settings > Privacy > App security > Screen security. Signal cannot block screenshots on macOS 27. However, users can add Signal to their Excluded Apps list via System Settings > Siri, which at least limits proactive access to conversations by Siri AI.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Alongside delivering enhancements specifically aimed at Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, Where Winds Meet, and Assetto Corsa Rally, 621.40 lists dealing with the fact "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background" as one of its key aims.
  • In a recent development, as to whether or not it's achieved that, some folks on Reddit and the Nvidia forum look to be making yes-shaped noises, but I'd not quite classify what I've seen so far as 100% proof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that nvidia may have finally released a proper cure for their last graphics driver, 621.24, reportedly writing unneccesarily vast amounts of data to some owners' SSDs. A hotfix late last week seemed to have made things better, but not fixed everything. Here's hoping driver 621.40 has managed to totally rectify things.

Alongside delivering enhancements specifically aimed at Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, Where Winds Meet, and Assetto Corsa Rally, 621.40 lists dealing with the fact "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background" as one of its key aims.

In a recent development, as to whether or not it's achieved that, some folks on Reddit and the Nvidia forum look to be making yes-shaped noises, but I'd not quite classify what I've seen so far as 100% proof. If you've reverted to the last driver which looked issue free, 621.01, waiting a few more days and seeing if a more definitive consensus emerges might be the best option.

After all, the hotfix which preceded 621.40 also declared war against those excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg, and it ended up stopping the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reducing the amount that's written, but not totally getting rid of the problem if an affected PC was left running for extended periods. At the very least, the fact the attempts at fixing the issue have now made their way into Nvidia's main branch is a key step towards the latest driver to hit the company's site and app eventually being excessive write-free.

According to recent reports, as we've noted in our previous coverage of the concern, which doesn't seem to be affecting all machines, if you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's writing little scraps of MB or substantial bits of GB.

  • "Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post.
  • Industry observers note that while the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)".

Industry observers note that while the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some notable scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.".

Sources indicate that deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox stated he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible.".

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

In a recent development, "Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way".

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence.".

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

We don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

In a recent development, you can find this car inside the Sunrise Premium Autos showroom at the north tip of Southside, southwest of Pay 'N' Spray - Salton or east across the road from Ron Gas - Southside. This region is to the northeast of Hamlet.

Recent findings suggest that there are two showrooms here, so make sure you have the right one, though the other does contain Pfister Growlers, in case you haven't gotten that car for Randy yet, either. Head inside to find the car—if you've played previous GTAs, you'll recognise it as a convertible with a white stripe down the middle. Hop inside, use the key cloner, and drive it through the glass.

This might damage it a bit, but you can always repair it at Ron Gas nearby, or at the gas station near Randy's shop. Just remember to drive fast, and if the tracker starts to beep, speed up to stop it pinging your location to the cops. Delivering this one gets you 6,500k and a 5k condition bonus as usual if it's in good nick.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar hired a former Gran Turismo pro to help master the car handling in GTA 6.
  • Lewis Bentley, a 2018 GT World Series Finalist, indicates he spent the last three-and-a-half years with the studio’s physics team, working on how the cars feel to drive.
  • In a now-deleted YouTube video – watched by GT Planet – he indicates he helped “put the auto in Grand Theft Auto”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar hired a former Gran Turismo pro to help master the car handling in GTA 6.

Lewis Bentley, a 2018 GT World Series Finalist, indicates he spent the last three-and-a-half years with the studio’s physics team, working on how the cars feel to drive.

In a now-deleted YouTube video – watched by GT Planet – he indicates he helped “put the auto in Grand Theft Auto”. He’s credited as a developer on the Physics Development Group, and he noted in his video that the entire team was “amazing”.

The Edinburgh-based dev is no stranger to real-life racing, as it fielded its own winning team in the 24 Hours of Nürburgring event four years ago. Ben Lyons, who made up part of the squad, was the Technical Director in charge of physics on the title.

I personally really love the way cars feel in the game.

Each type has its own distinctive handling model, and you can really feel the difference when you go to a Mod Shop and tune your car to taste.

It doesn’t have the distinctive heavy handling of GTA 4, but it’s also not quite as arcadey as GTA 5 either – I’d say it sits somewhere comfortably between the two, which is a good place to be.

I love all the extra work that’s been put into the DualSense’s haptic feedback, too; the way you can physically feel the change of grip between the different road surfaces – it’s impressive stuff.

Sources indicate that I just wish Rockstar had put a little more energy into the races themselves, because they do rely on aggressive rubber banding, which is pretty frustrating. Considering how meticulously the rest of the game is crafted, it would have been nice if a bit more thought went into this aspect.

In a recent development, all in all, though, I’m not surprised to learn GTA 6 had real-life race car drivers and pro Gran Turismo players on its team. You spend a good chunk of your time in Leonida driving, and I think by and large Rockstar really nailed this key aspect of the game.

Two Budget Smartwatches That Make Perfect Gifts

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1478 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you or someone on your shopping list wants a upcoming smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from.
  • In a recent development, luckily, you do have options.
  • Recent findings suggest that contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you or someone on your shopping list wants a upcoming smartwatch, you have plenty of options to choose from. The problem is, a lot of them can be quite pricey. Apple's cheapest smartwatch, the SE 3, starts at $249, and its other selections only skyrocket from there. On the flip side, the risk in picking a smartwatch that's too inexpensive is that the manufacturer likely made a series of sacrifices to get the price that low. At a certain point, the tradeoff just isn't worth it.

In a recent development, luckily, you do have options. There are two smartwatches on the market that aren't just cheaper than the competition, they're not even in the same ballpark. And while you shouldn't expect the same capabilities as you would on flagship wearables, these devices are perfectly usable, both as fitness trackers and smartwatches—all while spending well below $100 a pop. CNET put both smartwatches through their paces to make these determinations, so you know whichever model you get, you won't be picking up a wearable paperweight.

Recent findings suggest that contrary to what you might expect, Amazfit has no ties to Amazon—other than that you can buy these watches from the latter. Amazfit is its own company, and produces a wide selection of smartwatch options. The Bip 6 happens to be the company's latest budget smartwatch, with an MSRP of just $79.99. In most cases, a price that low would be a red flag for a smartwatch, but not in the Bip 6's case.

Sources indicate that the Amazfit Bip 6 holds its own against other flagship smartwatches. That's true on a surface level: This watch looks your average smartwatch, rather than a cheap imitation. In fact, at first glance, I'd bet most people would assume the Bip 6 is actually an Apple Watch. It has a rounded square design with a large 1.97-inch display with a resolution of 390 by 450 pixels (though there's no Always-On display). This isn't a cheap display, either: Amazfit put an AMOLED screen on the watch, which looks great indoors—though CNET Labs struggled to see the screen in direct sunlight.

Industry observers note that where the Bip 6 really shines, however, is with fitness tracking. This watch supports GPS, which makes tracking outdoor runs possible without a smartphone. CNET Labs found that it takes about 10 seconds to find a GPS signal, but once it connects, you're set. While running, the Bip 6 reliably tracks your heart rate. CNET Labs compared its sensor to the Polar chest strap HR monitor and found it on par, though, like other smartwatches, the Bip 6 is slower at detecting heart rate spikes. You'll get data like cadence and stride while tracking runs, and strength training and muscle groups while working out indoors. For example, CNET Labs found that it correctly identified arm muscle exercises while testing the watch during a pilates session.

It has been revealed that you also get some health and wellness features, too. The Bip 6 can measure heart rate variations, body temperature changes, sleep stages, and even your breathing quality. Its One Tap Measuring mode supports a single reading for heart rate, SpO2 (blood oxygen saturation), stress, and breathing rate, and it supports cycle tracking—though CNET specifies it can't track skin temperature like other smartwatches and health trackers. There's an optional subscription that provides AI coaching tools and looks out for health conditions like sleep apnea and insomnia. While health and wellness tracking is solid, note that CNET Labs found Amazfit's app, Zepp, to be confusing, since it simply displays your data without much context or explanation.

According to recent reports, for an $80 smartwatch, the Bip 6 has an excellent battery life. CNET Labs found that the watch could be pushed to its limits—multiple workouts using GPS, heart rate tracking, keeping the display on during workouts—and still run for eight days before needing a charge. In fact, reviewer Vanessa Hand Orellana speculates you could push the Bip 6 to Amazfit's two-week battery life claim by limiting some of the most intensive settings and features. The only downside here is that there is no fast charging, so it will take about two hours to get back to 100%. But if you're only charging the watch once every week or two, that isn't much of a burden. There's also no charger in the box, so you'll need to use a separate USB-C cable.

As a smartwatch, the Bip 6 can be a mixed bag. CNET found that the UI was clunky and sluggish, and the OS requires some user intervention before it's as usable as a standard Apple Watch or Galaxy Watch. While the watch has a voice assistant, Flow, CNET found it to be borderline unusable. However, CNET claims Android users can reply to texts with a keyboard or dictation without needing the assistant. iPhone users can't do the same by default, but by downloading a third-party app, they can jerry-rig the watch to send and receive texts.

Based on CNET Labs' testing, the Amazfit Bip 6 is one of the best budget smartwatches you can buy. For $80, you get a reliable workout tracker that looks like most standard watches on the market. And while you're making some sacrifices at this price point, they're largely worth it for $80.

While the Amazfit is a good choice for both iPhone and Android owners, the Galaxy Fit 3 might be the best choice for Samsung users. This isn't an option for iPhone users, and while it works with all Android devices, you get some Samsung-specific perks if you have a Galaxy phone.

Sources indicate that the Galaxy Fit 3 is even cheaper than the Amazfit Bip 6: This watch is only $60, which makes it among the cheapest smartwatches you can buy. Now, this doesn't look like your average smartwatch. Samsung opted for a fitness tracker-like design, with a long 1.6-inch (40mm) AMOLED display. But for a fitness tracker/smartwatch hybrid, it's a solid look.

In CNET's testing, one of the Galaxy Fit 3's biggest strengths is its battery life—though it pales in comparison to the Bip 6. When pushed to its limits, the Fit 3 can run three days in between charges, though Samsung claims you can get it up to 13 days with the right settings. While the Amazfit has it beat, the Fit 3 might sound like a dream compared to other smartwatches, even from Samsung. Unlike the Bip 6, the Fit 3 supports fast charging. You can fill the watch up completely in just over an hour.

Recent findings suggest that CNET did find that the "smart" elements of this wearable were a bit lacking, however. The Fit 3 doesn't support voice dictation or mobile payments like other watches do, and unless you have a Galaxy phone, you won't be able to access the camera remote or sync your alarms. And while the Amazfit Bip 6's "Flow" is hardly reliable, the Fit 3 doesn't have an assistant at all. You can see incoming calls and decline (but not answer) them, and you can send prewritten responses to text messages, but not initiate them. Still, CNET found that Samsung added the essentials: You have an alarm, calculator, weather app, camera remote, and, of course, the Samsung Health app. (What kind of health tracker would this be without it?).

In a recent development, CNET found that the Fit 3 is a reliable fitness tracker, particularly for $60. You can track over 100 different workouts, and the watch automatically logs exercises like runs, walks, rowing, and elliptical sessions—if you enable auto-tracking, that is. It also supports swimming with its IP68 water resistance rating. CNET Labs found that the heart rate tracking was "generally accurate" when compared to the Polar chest strap, though its slower with registering heart rate spikes. Interestingly, the heart rate tracker was a bit delayed in testing, but once CNET reviewed the data in the health app, the data had corrected to be largely accurate. You also get high and low heart rate alerts, though no ECG app. (The $249 Apple Watch SE 3 also omits this feature.).

It has been revealed that in CNET's testing, the sleep tracker on the Fit 3 was useful, if not entirely accurate. The watch can detect your sleep stages and look out for snoring using your Galaxy phone's mic. Like other health trackers, you get a sleep score, but CNET found it a bit inaccurate, since it rated a six and a half hour sleep session "Excellent" (91/100).

Sources indicate that still, the Fit 3 is really the only other smartwatch option at this price point that people should seriously consider. Until another tech giant drops a product around this MSRP, you have two solid choices in the Amazfit Bip 6 and Galaxy Fit 3.

"Clearly not everything has gone well" during Fable's lengthy creation, says Playground boss, but the "original vision" remains intact despite taking cues from other RPGs

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that the Fable reboot is finally set to kick the release chicken (I'm not sure that's an established phrase anywhere in the world, but roll with it) early next year, following a not small amount of time in development and multiple delays.
  • I say this with some pride – tempered against the fact that this has been obviously an enormously long development, so clearly not everything has gone well – but I would say that our original vision of what Fable needs to be has remained unchanged," Ralph Fulton, one of Playground's co-founders, told our suit-wearing siblings at GIBiz.
