📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Fable reboot is finally set to kick the release chicken (I'm not sure that's an established phrase anywhere in the world, but roll with it) early next year, following a not small amount of time in development and multiple delays. Despite that long time in the oven having made it necessary to look beyond just the series' classic entries for RPG inspiration, Playground Games' Fable general manager has said the team's "original vision" of what a Fable game needs to be hasn't changed.

I say this with some pride – tempered against the fact that this has been obviously an enormously long development, so clearly not everything has gone well – but I would say that our original vision of what Fable needs to be has remained unchanged," Ralph Fulton, one of Playground's co-founders, told our suit-wearing siblings at GIBiz.

"There are many reasons that this game development has been long," he added. "It's a upcoming team, it's a new genre, a new franchise, new technology – although we're building in an engine that we know well. It's also because a Fable game must have a great story with memorable characters and high-stakes drama, and also it needs to be funny and to have that British wit infused throughout it. Then there's combat, the quest structure, and the world of Albion and its people, and the simulations that underpin it. You'd be nuts to take on all of that in the first project, and yet here we are.".

In a recent development, fulton went on to note that despite that, Playground have worked to ensure their game's scope hasn't grown ever wider as they've made it. One call made early on with the social and economic simming that goes with the likes of landlording and being a dick to entire villages was that the studio "would only model first and second degree ripple effects", due to feeling that "players would only notice or we could only communicate the consequences up to the second degree". That makes sense, not every game can or should be a strategy game like Civ, wherein seeing your actions cause or influence a thousand different tidal waves over time is part of the central appeal. Not every game also has the budget of a GTA 6, which works deep simulation mechanics into a crime adventure, but feels like an exception to the rules even compared to Xbox-backed games like Fable.

On the other hand, Fulton did make clear that Playground have looked beyond the original entries in the series for RPG inspiration, fearing their game might be left behind if not. "Principally, technology has advanced," he said when asked what's changed while the game's been in the works. "In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard. And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG.

"All of these games continue to reset player expectations, which means I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects.".

We've already seen some of the ways in which the reboot diverges from its older forebears. As far as I'm concerned, albeit as someone with only a brief dalliance in the classic Fables, such tweaks could go either way. It is interesting to see Assassin's Creed mentioned alongside The Witcher 3 as having changed the RPG game. A game like Baldur's Gate 3 or even Starfield would strike me as a more obvious candidate to point to, so the AC mention might offer some indiction of the direction Playground have taken with their design.

It has been revealed that fable is, of course, being backed by Microsoft. The manufacturer are subject to an ongoing boycott by the BDS movement and have inflicted significant layoffs on their Xbox studios this year. As for whether the latter upheaval has affected Playground or Xbox's backing of Fable, Fulton offered a rather nothing answer here about Forza Horizon being good for the studio and the importance of keeping everyone internally in the loop as to how work on the game's going.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought.
  • An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit.
  • Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

"The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects.".

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

Sources indicate that in just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, noted in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

As for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token.".

It has been revealed that rockstar has not confirmed a PC version of GTA 6, but the company has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report noted GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

According to recent reports, these latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Analyst estimates have put GTA 6 at 53 million copies sold, which, if accurate, places it as the 13th best-selling game of all time after just a week.

In the least surprising bit of news of 2026, GTA 6 is selling pretty well. It was probably the most anticipated game ever and is the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic, so naturally the sales have followed. The first official number from Rockstar Games placed it at 32.5 million copies sold before it was even released, which had made it the 30th best-selling game ever above the likes of Super Mario Odyssey, Monster Hunter World, and Elden Ring. But that was just pre-release, so it's no shock to say that its fortunes haven't ended there.

Alinea Analytics' head of market analysis, Rhys Elliott, posts the latest estimate over on Twitter, which places Rockstar's latest at 53 million copies sold, making $4.7 billion in its first week.

If this number is accurate, GTA 6 is the 13th best-selling game ever, with it unseating Animal Crossing: New Horizons, and overtaking the likes of Cyberpunk 2077, The Sims, and the Pokemon Generation 1 games (which have a combined sales figure of 47.44 million across Red, Blue and Yellow).

Sources indicate that GTA 6 has sold 53M copies (75.7% on PS5) after a week on the market (@alineaanalytics estimates). Some other quick stats from our estimates: - It's made $4.7B (76.1% on PS5, due to regional prices) - 7M players have already played for over 50 hours. - 250K folks have played for over 100 hours (!!!!) - The US accounts for 33.5% of PS5's GTA 6 copies. Publishing another substantial deep dive on Substack shortly.November 27, 2026.

Elliott's data also estimates that just under a quarter of GTA 6 sales were on Xbox, with the Series X|S version accounting for 13 million vs PS5's 40 million. And it's not like it's just selling well either, as he reckons that seven million players have already played over 50 hours, with 250k of those having already played 100 hours. For reference, the game had been out in New Zealand around 219 hours at the time the tweet was posted.

Obviously, this is massively impressive no matter how you look at it. But it's worth keeping in mind that the PC release hasn't even dropped yet, so this has the potential to skyrocket once more when PC players – and console players who are going to double dip – get their hands on it.

Three Reasons Not to Use ‘Buy Now, Pay Later’ During Black Friday

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1121 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales.
  • Industry observers note that while BNPL plans can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any significant discounts.
  • Recent findings suggest that to be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the company is not uniquely misleading on this front.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that gone are the days of needing to wait until after Thanksgiving to shop some seriously substantial Black Friday sales. As you're adding item after item to your cart during the sale, you might be tempted by offers for an "affordable monthly payment system." Also known as "buy now, pay later" (BNPL), the pitch is a tempting one: Buy what you need now, and pay later, "on your own timeline." But as convenient as it sounds, you should think twice before using buy now, pay later options, whether during Black Friday, Cyber Monday, or at any other time.

Industry observers note that while BNPL plans can allow you to pay for purchases in installments without interest, they come with a cost that can easily outweigh any significant discounts. Let's take a look at the hidden costs of BNPL, and why you're better off paying upfront for all your Black Friday purchases.

Recent findings suggest that to be clear, Amazon doesn't have its own buy now, pay later program, and the company is not uniquely misleading on this front. The process is straightforward: you choose your items, select Affirm (a third-party lender) at checkout, complete a quick application, and receive an instant decision on your loan terms. Individual transactions initiated through Affirm are limited to $25,000, with a daily maximum of $100,000 across multiple purchases—but of course, your Black Friday splurge will be nowhere near that big, right? (Right?!).

The main draw of these programs is the ability to "pay at your own pace." If you are required to pay a down payment, that is due at the time of the transaction. From there, your first monthly payment is usually due one month after your purchase is processed. Each following payment will be due one month later, on the same day of the month.

Sources indicate that you can choose your own timeline, usually spanning 3, 6, 12, or 24 months, depending on the purchase amount and your creditworthiness. Unlike traditional credit cards, Affirm shows you the exact payment amount and total cost upfront, and claims no hidden fees or compound interest.

You need a separate Affirm account in addition to your Amazon Prime membership. The application process requires basic information, including your name, mobile phone number, date of birth, and the last four digits of your Social Security number. Affirm performs a soft credit check initially, which doesn't impact your credit score, though they may conduct a hard inquiry for some loans.

BNPL looks are helpful if you really need to finance something significant, but whenever possible, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses.

The ease of this sort of financing can make expensive purchases feel more affordable than they actually are. When you can buy a $1,000 tablet for "just $67 per month," it's easy to lose sight of the total cost, as well as your overall financial picture. In turn, this makes it all too easy to overspend on items you might not have purchased otherwise. You're better off taking a breath, stepping away from your shopping cart, and setting alerts to be notified when a product hits a price you can stomach, at a time you can afford it.

Sources indicate that despite what you may have heard in the past, BNPL providers may report to credit bureaus, meaning your BNPL purchases can in fact affect your credit score. For instance, all Affirm payments (including on-time, late, and missed payments) are now reported to the credit bureau Experian. So if you miss payments or default on the installment proposal, it will cause damage to your credit score—making it even harder to get approved for mortgages, auto loans, credit cards, and other financing down the road.

Still, not all BNPL providers report to credit bureaus or use the same type of credit check, so it’s key to understand the specific terms and practices of any service you’re considering.

When you use a credit card, you get valuable purchase protections like extended warranty coverage, price protection, and the ability to dispute fraudulent charges. BNPL looks generally don't come with these safeguards. This means you're on the hook if something goes wrong with your BNPL purchase and the retailer doesn't make things right. The smarter move is to only buy what you can afford during a sale, no matter how tempting those deals may seem.

It has been revealed that although installment plans are helpful if you really need to finance something major, it’s best to avoid taking on debt for everyday expenses. Better to wait for a good price for something you truly need and can afford to pay for right now.

If there's a big-ticket item on sale for Black Friday but it's still out of your budget, consider these two questions before you turn to BNPL through Affirm:.

Recent findings suggest that is this really an essential purchase? BNPL should really only be used on completely necessary purchases that you can’t afford right now, but can afford in six weeks. On that note...

Will I be able to pay this off within six weeks? When a bigger payment gets broken down into smaller installments, you might find yourself overspending in the long run, because it "feels" like you can afford it. Stay on top of how much you’re actually spending—especially if you're considering multiple BNPL purchases—and how it will impact your overall budget going forward.

For more information about deals and discounts, keep an eye on all of Lifehacker's Black Friday coverage.

Industry observers note that in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft, they of the recently revealed generative AI-focused game studio Motherbrain, have denied they're forcing upcoming games being pitched by their developers to integrate use of genAI as a rule. The publishers' statement comes in the wake of a report claiming that Ubisoft devs with pitches that don't use genAI are required to explain in detail why they've decided it isn't suitable for the game being outlined.

The report from Vertical Slice cited anonymous Ubisoft staff as having said that the publishers' game pitching process now requires devs to either outline how they'll use generative AI to speed up production, or offer a specific justification as to why the tech isn't being used.

Sources indicate that ubisoft management reportedly revealed the change during a presentation to staff, with one source telling Vertical Slice that the company are all in on generative AI. They cited an "attitude shift" among Ubisoft management as having left workers feeling "cornered by generative AI all the time", but made clear Ubisoft haven't brought in a blanket mandate forcing devs to use genAI no matter what.

In a recent development, ubisoft have emphasised the latter in a statement subsequently issued to Vertical Slice. "We encourage our teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work," the organization wrote. "This doesn’t mean that projects are required to use generative AI. Teams need to determine whether, and how, these technologies make sense for the game they want to make and the experience they want to create for players.".

It has been revealed that ubisoft have been keen on experimenting with genAI in game development for a little while - something essentially set in stone by the establishing of Motherbrain as a proper division where the organization can work on the likes of the "first playable generative AI experience" they were shouting about earlier this year. That move came in a year Ubisoft have spent vast swaths of laying off staff and closing studios, as part of a restructuring they kicked off with a barrage of cancellations in January.

Sources indicate that most recently, those cuts hit 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on a list of other affected subsidiaries that I'm very much getting tired of wheeling out whenever Ubisoft inevitably insist on adding to it.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.
  • "Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report.
  • The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: latest management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

"Sources close to Microsoft's plans tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," says the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free strategy was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: latest management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

Recent findings suggest that if Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games.".

Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it debuted on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that the Emperor’s Upcoming Groove is one of those Walt Disney Animation movies that will forever and always be imprinted in my brain.
  • It has been revealed that the animation movie landscape has changed a lot over the years.
  • I was the last guy to do a Disney movie where they said it was ‘an honor’, and that’s why I didn’t get a lot of money.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the Emperor’s Upcoming Groove is one of those Walt Disney Animation movies that will forever and always be imprinted in my brain. The 2000 film came out at just the right time in my childhood when I’d put it on repeat. I could honestly quote most of it front to back. However, I had no idea about the experience Kuzco's voice actor, David Spade, had.

It has been revealed that the animation movie landscape has changed a lot over the years. These days all the significant roles go to Hollywood names rather than talents known specifically for voice acting. David Spade, who famously got his start on SNL, spoke to this while talking about The Emperor’s Newly introduced Groove with these words:.

I was the last guy to do a Disney movie where they said it was ‘an honor’, and that’s why I didn’t get a lot of money. And then, they came out with Shrek, and everyone got $5 million bucks, and I go 'Wait, what the fuck is going on?'.

It has been revealed that hey, he makes a good point. Prior to the 21st Century, animated movies weren't paying major-name celebrities the big bucks. David Spade was also working with Disney Animation at a time when the studio wasn’t making blockbusters to the degree it is now with the likes of Frozen or Moana. Spade even disclosed how much he made, saying this:.

I got $75,000, which sounds like a lot. It was a lot… They rat fucked me.

Industry observers note that shrek came out in 2001 – one year after The Emperor’s New Groove – and made almost half a billion worldwide. It helped usher in an era of blockbuster animated films led by A-list celebrities that we continue to live in. The Emperor's New Groove made $169 million worldwide, and was actually thought of as a commercial flop at the time of its release.

According to recent reports, spade’s comments about The Emperor’s Newly introduced Groove were made while on his podcast Fly On The Wall with guest Denis Leary, who famously plays Diego the saber-tooth tiger in the Ice Age movies. Ice Age came out a couple of years after Spade’s Disney movie, and has a sixth installment among upcoming Disney movies in 2027. Leary mentioned he and the rest of the Ice Age cast have received pay bumps since first signing up to the franchise because they are watched so frequently on streaming.

Even though I imagine it’s a bummer that Spade lost out on some cash he might have gotten for the same amount of work a couple of years later on something else, he also made a point of saying he loves The Emperor’s New Groove and how well it turned out. But he did so while pointing out something else about being a voice actor on a Disney film that was hard to deal with in the moment….

No, I did it and it just kept going and going, and I’m like, ‘Guys, I don’t want to drive out to Disney every day and just lay down an hour or two of tracks. I’m like Denis Leary, I have shit to do on my day off. I love the movie now, but during it I was starting to get a little itchy. Like, there’s no ending. I really love it, and they’re miracle workers with the freaking animation.

Sources indicate that animated movies like The Emperor’s New Groove famously go through a long production process. The 2000 movie in particular did so because it was actually originally an entirely different movie called Kingdom of the Sun. It was more inspired by The Prince and the Pauper, featured Owen Wilson in a voice role, and Spade was playing a character named Manco instead of Kuzco before they shifted directions. No wonder he was getting antsy while making it!

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

While I can understand David Spade’s blunt thoughts about working with Disney, I’m so happy he stuck it out and played Kuzco. The movie has brought me so much joy throughout my life, and it’s certainly one of the most beloved projects of his career. You can watch it now with a Disney+ subscription.

According to recent reports, finally, this failure is all the more significant because it has happened across lines of gender privilege. RPS has a full-time staff of cisgender men, which inevitably gives rise to bias and ignorance we must actively confront, while we work towards being in a position to address our lack of gender diversity, beyond commissioning the occasional marginalised freelance writer. Non-cisgender writers are both much more exposed to abuse and much less favoured in terms of steady work. As such, a public rebuke from your own editor is far more damaging than it would be if the freelancer were a cisgender man. On this count, I have been extremely thoughtless in ways that would likely not have been the case when this site had a majority female editorship.

Ashley, I am deeply sorry that I let you down in these ways.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that 25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union stated, while 75% voted against it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After two weeks of voting that bracketed the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games employees have voted overwhelmingly against a recognition agreement with the IWGB Game Workers Union.

Industry observers note that 25% of Rockstar employees voted in favor of the recognition agreement, the union stated, while 75% voted against it. 1,544 employees took part in the vote, representing a turnout of just over 93%.

It has been revealed that rockstar workers actually founded a union earlier this year—the Rockstar Game Workers Union, a subsidiary of the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain—and it will continue to operate as it has. The IWGB said the outcome will not prevent Rockstar workers from organizing or exercising union rights, but the company will not be required to regularly meet with union representatives for collective bargaining or other relevant matters.

Despite the vote, the union stated it will continue with organizing efforts at Rockstar.

"For anyone at Rockstar who believes in a fairer workplace, a fairer sector and a fairer society—this isn’t a sign to retreat, it’s a sign to double down on what we stand for. Hundreds of our coworkers voted in favour of our union at Rockstar, yet sadly we recognize we have more work to do to build understanding and win the trust of more of our colleagues," the IWGB Rockstar Game Workers Union stated. "We’re ready to put in the effort to make that happen.

"Whilst we haven’t emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for fresh kinds of conversation to start happening. People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We heard from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions can lead us.".

The power to shape our working lives has always been, and always will be, in our hands.

In a separate statement, Rockstar head of publishing Jennfer Kolbe remarked the studio is "extraordinarily proud of our team, the culture we've built together and the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6.".

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews.

Recent findings suggest that "This result reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong," Kolbe stated. "As we look ahead, we're excited to build on all we've accomplished together.".

It has been revealed that rockstar, which said it worked with the IWGB to ensure employees were able to make an informed decision in a fair and transparent vote, came under fire in October 2025 for firing more than 30 employees, all of whom were members of a private trade union Discord channel. The IWGB called it "the most ruthless act of union busting in the history of the UK games industry," while Rockstar notes they were fired for leaking information about "upcoming and unannounced games." That matter is now before an employment tribunal; closing submissions were made last week.

#154895. "This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1473 w)

"This isn't a sign to retreat": Rockstar's historic union vote has failed, with 75% voting against, but the organisers are going to "keep fighting"

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1473 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have revealed.
  • According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives.".
  • It has been revealed that speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the potentially historic vote at GTA 6 creators Rockstar Games on whether to seek formal union recognition has failed, the International Workers of Great Britain have revealed. Around 1600 studio members cast ballots across 12th to 26th November, even as the firm's open world Bonnie & Clyde 'em up released onto PlayStation and Xbox storefronts. In the end, approximately 25% of the participants voted in favour.

According to the IWGB themselves, "the result does not prevent Rockstar workers from organising with the IWGB or exercising their trade union rights, but means management will not be formally committed to regular meetings with union representatives.".

It has been revealed that speaking to RPS in an emailed statement, Rockstar's head of publishing Jennifer Kolbe argued that the vote's failure "reflects our team's strong support for continuing the direct relationships, collaboration and open dialogue that have helped make Rockstar Games so innovative and strong." The IWGB, meanwhile, have declared that "this isn't a sign to retreat, it's a sign to double down on what we stand for". They're going to keep mobilising for more labour power, with the failed vote now framed as a foot in the door.

"Whilst we haven't emerged with a recognition deal, this ballot has put our union on the radar of every worker, and opened the door for fresh kinds of conversation to start happening," reads the union statement. "People entirely unfamiliar with unions were for the first time debating employment conditions, collective bargaining rights, and our contracts. We head from many more colleagues about what mattered to them, and we hope people will continue to engage so that we can see where these new discussions will lead us.

Recent findings suggest that "A recognition agreement would have marked a path towards greater workplace democracy," they continue. "But it's one route of many. At Rockstar we have already won, and will continue to win, tangible changes that improve our everyday lives. We'll keep fighting for a say. For pay transparency, contractual overtime pay, and protections against AI and layoffs.".

The Rockstar UK unionisation drive has been a long journey. The vote follows open confrontation between Rockstar management in the UK and IWGB-affiliated Rockstar employees working out of a private Discord server. After allegedly keeping the Discord server under surveillance for over two years, Rockstar bosses fired around 30 staff in October 2026 on charges of "gross misconduct" and breach of confidentiality. The IWGB and the fired workers have countered by accusing Rockstar of union-busting, observing that the Discord's putative union membership had reached the 10% minimum required for statutory recognition under UK law, shortly before the firings.

Recent findings suggest that 220 Rockstar staff subsequently signed an open letter to management calling for the reinstatement of the fired workers. The IWGB also organised protest rallies outside the offices of Rockstar North in Edinburgh and Take-Two Interactive in London. A UK Member of Parliament weighed in, calling on ministers to "stop this from happening again". Finally, the ousted workers took Rockstar to court in an employment tribunal that has run for much of this year: the closing statements landed on the eve of GTA 6's release, with a judge's verdict pending.

Industry observers note that I'm sorry to see the union vote fall through, given the boost a formally recognised GTA developer union in the UK would have given to labour organisation across the industry. In the short term, of course, it might have made for a safer and more supportive workplace at Rockstar. While there is relatively little recent reporting on current working conditions, many Rockstar games are allegedly the product of "crunch culture", stemming back to the development of the first 3D Grand Theft Autos on PS2.

In January 2010, an anonymous user posting on behalf of the “wives of Rockstar San Diego employees" claimed that staff had been forced to work 12-hour, six day weeks to finish the first Red Dead Redemption. A landmark report from Kotaku in 2018, based on interviews with 34 current and 43 former employees, described developers piling up evening and weekend work across Rockstar's empire, with crunch especially severe among QA staff at Rockstar Lincoln in the UK.

Some of Kotaku's sources said they had been explicitly pushed to work overtime by managers, facilitated by workplace systems such as hour-logging. Others spoke of a more vaporous expectation that they put in inhuman effort, because after all, working at the studio behind GTA is a privilege. Many had fond memories of their experiences, even as they acknowledged the toll taken on their minds, bodies and relationships outside work. This is part of the problem with crunch - it doesn't have to be explicitly imposed. It comes about because some creative and enthusiastic people are not good at recognising their own limits, and less scrupulous employers are happy to profit from this and, worse, erect a working culture around it.

The 2018 Kotaku piece acknowledges that some crunch results from the uneven and unpredictable way many videogames are made, but it also talks about overtime brought on by unaccountable leadership, with studio co-founders Dan and Sam Houser "renowned for rebooting, overhauling, and discarding large chunks of their games." (Dan Houser left the firm in 2020.) The same heads were also said to value the "appearance" of developers going the extra mile, with one dev telling the site they were encouraged to walk a lap of the office on Saturday, whenever the Housers were in town. Together with anxieties about confidentiality, that emphasis on devs being visibly busy perhaps informs Rockstar's cancelling of hybrid working in early 2024, which precipitated some of this year's union activism.

In a recent development, many of the people pushing for unionisation at Rockstar are also reacting to events across the games industry. There has been a huge wave of mass layoffs as companies "adjust" following the boom period initiated by Covid lockdowns. Some of those laid off had recently shipped commercially successful games, like Battlefield 6. GTA 6 developers have publicly expressed concerns about getting cut, even as their new open worlder makes sales records.

According to recent reports, A chunk of the recent mass layoffs are owing to lucrative manufacturer acquisitions and consolidations that have attracted criticism from existing unions. Microsoft have spent two years axing studios, projects and jobs after spending around $69 billion to acquire Activision Blizzard. EA are now owned by a consortium led by Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund and Donald Trump's son-in-law; the company has since laid off hundreds of developers and closed the mighty BioWare as they shoulder an enormous debt, which they're reportedly hoping to offset by means of mass generative AI-powered costcutting. As alluded to in today's IWGB statement, there is the overarching question of how genAI - often explicitly mandated by executives - will threaten livelihoods by automating tasks, giving bosses an excuse to keep headcounts small by one means or another.

It has been revealed that the repeated layoff waves have inspired a lot of union action at many large videogame companies, from Microsoft to Ubisoft, but I suspect a lot of that hasn't been apparent outside labour organising and enthusiast circles. GTA is as breakthrough a vidya as you can get. Rockstar forming a union would have been a foundation from which to talk more about worker power beyond the games industry.

As often when reporting on unionisation, I'm left idly wondering about what kind of art a fully unionised industry would create. The production conditions of many games can be deduced from their design – a photorealistic open world game, for example, is a vast assemblage of resources that may hinge on distributed development across an unequal world. Rockstar both represent AAA gaming at its grAAAndest, and have historically been part of the auteur craze, with the Housers having the final say on every detail.

Sources indicate that we are, in general, all very familiar with the caricatures of auteur-led development, positioned as a source of both eccentric brilliance and ruinous hubris. I think there's much less of a narrative for the kind of art you get from teams where workers have serious negotiating power, though there are precedents in the form of cooperatives and similar organisations that tether their labour conditions more boldly to the kind of art they produce: for example, Die Gute Fabrik, and most recently, Summer Eternal.

Industry observers note that A unionised Rockstar wouldn't just be a space in which workers are better protected against the expectations of managers and financial stakeholders; you'd get different kinds of art. Maybe more interesting kinds of art! I do wonder if union organisers could do a more effective job of expressing this hope, perhaps exploring where certain games have lost their way because workers were treated like cannon fodder.

According to recent reports, sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there. That's more than the official GTA 6 day-one sales tally of 32.5m copies across all platforms.

Unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation. According to the PlayStation Blog, the game has recorded the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation ever, surpassing any previous record across all kinds of game - multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player.

In addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales. GTA 6 is apparently the first game played on 70 percent of newly introduced PS5 consoles.

The average GTA 6 playtime, per person, is a considerable 17.4 hours, the blog states, and the total number of hours spent playing the game is 683 million - a number so high I can't contextualise it.

Sources indicate that microsoft hasn't declared equivalent data for Xbox but I assume the game is a record-breaker there, too, given that it broke pre-order Xbox Store records in the same way GTA 6 did on PlayStation. However, GTA 6 is estimated to have sold far more copies on PlayStation - as many as 75 percent of its total sales, according to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott.

Industry observers note that elliott estimated that GTA 6 amassed a colossal 44.9m sales by the end of its opening weekend, and that 33.7m of those were on PlayStation 5 (which still doesn't reach the '39 million unique players' stat Sony has just trotted out) and 11.2m were on Xbox. That amount of sales would earn Rockstar something like $4bn in revenue.

Industry observers note that the arrival of GTA 6 has, then, been seismic. The game has wowed critics and dominated conversation not only in the games industry but also across entertainment news and mainstream news. Meanwhile, however, we await the verdict in the Rockstar Games employment tribunal in Scotland, relating to the sudden firing of 34 employees a year ago. Was Rockstar union-busting, as alleged? It'll be a historic ruling if deemed so.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sales have been ramping up for several days.
  • Sources indicate that millions of Amazon Prime owners right now pay $14.99 per month or $139 per year for their memberships—though other aims cost less if you qualify.
  • If you’re on the fence about signing up for (or renewing) your Prime membership, here’s how to judge whether or not the benefits outweigh the $139 cost.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday isn't until Nov. 27, but Amazon's early Black Friday sales have been ramping up for several days. For frequent Amazon shoppers, Prime can quickly pay for itself—mostly thanks to the free shipping perk. But how does the math shake out if you aren't regularly ordering from Amazon? Is it worth signing up if you only shop during major sales?

Sources indicate that millions of Amazon Prime owners right now pay $14.99 per month or $139 per year for their memberships—though other aims cost less if you qualify. For example, the Amazon Prime Student program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

If you’re on the fence about signing up for (or renewing) your Prime membership, here’s how to judge whether or not the benefits outweigh the $139 cost.

Here are the main perks of Amazon Prime that make it worth the cost for so many consumers.

It has been revealed that free two-day shipping on millions of items: This is the main draw of Prime. If you shop frequently on Amazon and want quick free delivery, the shipping perks alone may make Prime worthwhile. Prime members also get free same-day delivery on over 3 million items in eligible areas. The ultra-fast (and morally suspect) shipping usually costs $9.99 per order for non-members, though you can choose lower-cost or free shipping options if you're willing to place larger orders and wait longer to receive them.

Access to Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV indicates, and Amazon Originals. If you ask me, the content library isn’t as robust as Netflix or Hulu, but this is still an added value.

Other Prime benefits: You also get Amazon Music for streaming songs, Prime Reading for ebooks, magazines, and audiobooks; Prime gaming, free photo storage, and occasional exclusive discounts/deals.

Recent findings suggest that amazon Prime Rewards Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon/Whole Foods purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the annual fee.

It has been revealed that number of people: Prime benefits can be shared with other members of your household. The more users, the more value per person.

Let's say you don't care about Prime Video, Amazon Music, or free e-books, and just want to know if you'll save money you would otherwise be spending on shipping.

Industry observers note that for non-Prime members, Amazon requires a minimum order of $35 to qualify for free shipping on eligible items. The average shipping costs for non-members aren't publicly listed, and can vary by item and shipping speed, typically ranging from $5 to $10.

Industry observers note that for our purposes, I messed around on my non-shared, non-Prime Amazon account to find an average shipping cost of around $6 per order (assuming the order total fell below the $35 threshold, of course). Of course, shipping costs will vary depending on the item and how promptly you want it, but let’s compare the cost to the appeal of Prime’s two-day shipping option. So, we have the cost of individual online orders (around six bucks) compared to the free delivery that comes with an $139 annual fee. This means the costs you’d save on shipping alone make Prime worth the cost as long as you place more than two dozen orders in a year.

In other words: The $139 annual fee pays for itself as long as you order from Amazon Prime at least twice a month.

Sources indicate that of course, this conclusion is strictly in terms of shipping costs. How it stacks up ethically is between you and the person in the mirror.

Industry observers note that and then there's this crucial caveat: You can still get free shipping from Amazon without a Prime membership, provided your order has $35 or more of eligible items. However, this won't grant you Prime shipping speed—your order will typically take five to eight days to be delivered. But you can place fewer, larger orders and wait a little longer, and still never pay for shipping.

Also worth considering is how much of that membership cost you'll be able to recoup via exclusive Prime Day offers. During the sale, some items will be heavily discounted only for Prime members—but whether the Prime Day price is really a "deal" will vary greatly based on the item you're buying. Some of those "significant discounts" aren't any greater than what the item typically sells for. The Prime Day price can even be higher than other sale prices throughout the year. That's why it's crucial to make sure what you're ordering is something you planned to buy anyway—and that the sale price is actually a true bargain—before you order.

According to recent reports, the cost of a Prime membership is a solid value for anyone using Amazon 23 times per year or more—especially if you're also watching indicates on Prime Video or purchasing something that is deeply discounted for Prime Day. But if you only shop on Amazon a few times a year and don't take advantage of Prime Day offers or the other benefits, then that $139 annual fee isn't necessarily paying for itself.

Recent findings suggest that yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

I’m on sub-level three of a long-abandoned rocket silo, reading heavily redacted files by flashlight. Most of the screen is black, save for a little pang of light from my torch, and my heart beats rapidly as I comb through reams of text on the right of the screen.

It’s not flashy nor is it a massive spectacle, and it’s taken me hours to get to this point. However, it may be one of the most engrossing gaming moments I’ve had on PS5 this year.

This game is Zero Parades: Director’s Cut, the spiritual successor to ZA/UM’s enormously praised Disco Elysium, which has finally made its way to PS5 after launching on PC earlier in 2026.

It’s a text-and-dice-based RPG, where Operant (read: spy) Cascade has returned to the town of Portofiro five years after an assignment went horribly wrong. This is her chance at redemption.

However, upon arriving in Portofiro, she finds her double comatose in their safe house, and with no clue as to what her assignment actually is, Cascade must take to the streets.

Industry observers note that what you’ll find there is a massive, sprawling collection of mysteries that weave and connect in myriad ways. A girl’s plea to help find her missing dad may link to a poetry magazine that could be a front. A cosmonaut figure in the bustling bazaar was my first thread that eventually led me to read through documents underground in the dark 20 hours later.

Industry observers note that admittedly, there are times that pacing is to its detriment. The opening hours are especially slow, as you get a lay of the land. However, like any good mystery thriller, I'm of the opinion you have to put in the time before you can reap those mysterious rewards. It's not going to be for everyone — which should be obvious with the whole text-and-dice-based RPG descriptor — however, if it is your thing, then your patience will pay off.

Industry observers note that zero Parades is a familiar game for anyone that played Disco Elysium, but it does have its own unique identity. There’s a lot of crossover, from the style of narration to the stacked-against-you odds of its dice-driven actions. However, where Disco is a more internal reflection of our initially nameless detective, Zero Parades sprinkles some of that in with a deal more narrative mystery, and I love that about it.

Cascade is basically a f*ck up, haunted by the elusive errors of her past, so while you may have the skill somewhere inside of you to be a good spy, it’s but a fleeting thing. It’s entirely down to how you level up Cascade, across the faculties of action, relation, and intelligence to define the kind of spy you are.

Kicking off my investigation, I pile a ton of points into intelligence skill, particularly Technoflex, the study of all things tech. Sometimes this skill is subtly useful, like being able to fix the fax machine in the photo printing store where my safe house is located. Other times, it proves its worth in major ways, like being able to bypass the security lock of a secret prison, because I am aware of a system flaw in that precise model.

Recent findings suggest that however, there is real flexibility to Zero Parades’ exploration and progression. For example, that secret prison has multiple ways in, and you may be able to talk yourself in via the front door if you have the right skills levelled up.

By the time you figure out your assignment, the narrative has laid the foundation for many different approaches, and each can take you on its own weird road through the streets of Portofiro, and your success down those roads is dependent on how you build up your character.

And let me be clear: you can simply fail in Zero Parades – it’s sort of the crux of the whole experience. Whether it’s a botched escape from a mysterious man, or completely messing up an attempt to construct a homemade gun, Zero Parades is brilliant at making it feel like the odds are stacked against you.

Industry observers note that that is emphasised all the more with the stress system. Across fatigue, anxiety, and delirium (which relate to your action, relation, and intelligence upgrades), certain actions will build up pressure in any three of these gauges. As it ascends, Cascade will be hit with nerfs of varying severity, and if the scale maxes out, it will refresh and deduct a skill point for its related skill group.

In a recent development, there are ways to juggle this, of course. Smoking cigarettes, eating sweets, or certain drinks can lower specific gauges whilst increasing others, and sleeping is possible to reduce all gauges but is time-locked. You are then able to exert yourself to increase the chances of hitting the required dice numbers, but this comes at the cost of increasing the scale of its related gauge.

Sources indicate that the whole experience becomes a balancing act while trying to figure out which gauge may still require space to carry out certain actions. Maybe you decide not to engage in some activity for fear of needing it in something more crucial. Or maybe you spend it all wanting to cover everything, and then suffer the consequences when you really need it in a pivotal story moment.

In a recent development, this whole system means I am vehemently aware of Cascade’s physical and mental state at pretty much all times across the story. It also means that no part of the game’s content is trivial, as it all ties into one and other, not just narratively but mechanically. What I do now directly impacts what I can do later.

By the time the credits rolled, my ending felt especially my own. My own failures, successes, and regrets. And it massively encourages me to go for another try, to hopefully unlock new avenues, level up in different areas, and maybe even finish successfully (I messed up badly).

Sources indicate that as you can tell, I am a massive fan of this game, but it doesn’t get everything right. For one, the writing is great, as you would hope for, but it lacks the same razor edge that Disco Elysium has in spades. Voice acting is generally brilliant, but at times it feels like a game doing its best Disco impression, with a yearning to be as edgy as possible.

I did come to like Cascade’s voice performance a lot more as I spent more time with it, but it undeniably lacks the same punch as Lenvel Brown’s dulcet tones as The Narrator in Disco Elysium.

It has been revealed that then we come to the PS5’s performance. I played this on both PS5 and PS5 Pro, and the performance is surprisingly bad. For 90% of the game, as you talk to various characters, it’s obviously not an issue – you’re mainly just looking at still screens as text moves down the right side. However, when you’re running around the town of Portofiro, the frame rate consistently tanks.

It’s a shame because the art style is quite gorgeous, as it somehow mixes a painterly art style with a simultaneously dull aesthetic. Like in the story, Portofiro is a town of stalled potential, left to rot over its beauty. DualSense haptics are also surprisingly great, albeit subtle. It really makes you feel like you're flicking through redacted documents with nuanced ripples at your fingertips.

It has been revealed that zero Parades: Director’s Cut is a dense and highly detailed text-based RPG, that moves at a painstakingly slow pace. However, it’s part of the magic of this story. It lacks the same authenticity as Disco Elysium, but manages to hold its own with a riveting mystery that very naturally unfolds.

In a recent development, it’s riveting when a small detail links back to the previously abandoned thread, and you feel like a spy yourself as you try to piece it all together. It lets you relish in the world and revel in the chaos, and as the credits rolled, I just wanted to jump back in and try it all over again.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for a little while now, and already players are showing off their skills when it comes to the game's many heists. Despite the challenges in getting away clean, some are proving it's possible.

According to recent reports, for one, sneaking into a bank while the vault is open and stuffing your bags full of marked bills is a tricky process of gradually making your way through rooms and taking out guards as quietly as possible. While the police in the clip below were called to an eventual breakout of violence, a lengthy getaway allowed for a cheeky payday of almost $100,000 in cash.

This crew really cracked a whole bank vault and walked out with almost $100K in GTA 6 💰🏦🚔😮‍💨 #gtavi #gta pic.twitter.com/pJyFXREBvY.

One especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come swiftly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3.

As you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

Industry observers note that this GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr.

Here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

According to recent reports, if you're looking to get your life of crime properly underway, you can read our GTA 6 robberies page for a breakdown on how it works. Alternatively, for a wider view of the game, our GTA 6 walkthrough is the way to go.

It has been revealed that the Witcher 3 Remastered continues to recieve tweaks ahead of the Songs of the Past expansion arriving next year to whisk Gerry from the River off on a fresh adventure. Following some bloomin' improvements in October, its latest patch does a bunch of skill and mutation balancing, alongside further technical tweaks and fixes for some funky bugs.

"Fixed an problem where Reforging the Mastercrafted or Grandmaster Feline armor gave Geralt an unusual hairstyle," reads the first of numerous notes in the visual section of patch 5.02's notes about weird stuff happening to Gerry's luscious mane. "Fixed an issue where Geralt could become bald after enabling HairWorks on PC or Xbox Play Anywhere and then continuing the game on Xbox via Cross Progression," reads another that sounds slightly more serious. "Fixed an issue where growing a beard with the Rabble-rouser hairstyle made Geralt's head invisible," reads a third, which takes the cake.

Recent findings suggest that there've also been instances of Gerry or NPCs missing their faces or "other body parts". The NPCs, bless them, have also had to deal with contracting "overly bright red areas on their legs" when moving through crowds. Oh, and a building near Novigrad's docks has been cheeklily disappearing whenever Geralt gets close to it. One would assume it's just a bit shy, though that's a tough thing to be when your location means people embarking and disembarking from ships are constantly walking past. To be honest, it also sounds like it could have been adapted into an extra contract for Gerry if CD Projekt had fancied. The studio have also "fixed an problem where installing and uninstalling mods could cause merchants' inventories, Geralt's inventory and storage to be emptied".

According to recent reports, beyond the giggle-worthy bug fixes, the most consequential aspect of the patch to my eye will likely be the tweaks to the power of certain skills and mutations, which folks may well be testing out if they're trying to settle on a new build before Songs of the Past. Those tweaks are as follows:.

Generally speaking, sign-heavy Gerry builds look like they'll be most acutely affected and be less effective following this patch. I typically only rely on Quen for a bit of shielding, because I'm an unimaginative monster slayer, so I'm not sure I'll notice it too much, but if you really make the most of your magical abilities it might hit your Gerry pretty hard.

It's worth skimming through the full notes if you've time, which also contain a few PC-specific fixes and tweaks. Starting a Hearts of Stone or Blood and Wine-only playthrough on Steam Deck should no longer lead to long load times, for example, while there've been some improvements made to path tracing and ray reconstruction .

#154885. I Tried Building My Own Interactive World in Google Genie, but Real-Time AI Engines Aren't There Yet

📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

I Tried Building My Own Interactive World in Google Genie, but Real-Time AI Engines Aren't There Yet

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (997 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, beyond the Gemini assistant, Gemini Notebook, and various other AI offerings, Google also develops Genie, a world-building engine intended to help you create immersive visual experiences and games using only text prompts.
  • Sources indicate that these promises point to the future of AI in all kinds of ways—from robotics to world sims—but the tool requires a lot of computing power, and access is limited for the time being.
  • Industry observers note that it's no exaggeration to say you can build an entire virtual world in Google Genie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, beyond the Gemini assistant, Gemini Notebook, and various other AI offerings, Google also develops Genie, a world-building engine intended to help you create immersive visual experiences and games using only text prompts. Think of them like AI videos you can interact with and move through.

Sources indicate that these promises point to the future of AI in all kinds of ways—from robotics to world sims—but the tool requires a lot of computing power, and access is limited for the time being. You can dive in now if you're on one of the Google AI Ultra aims ($99.99 or $199.99 a month), or join the waitlist if you're a Google AI Pro user ($19.99 a month). But if you've got access, is it worth the effort (and money)? I put it to the test.

Industry observers note that it's no exaggeration to say you can build an entire virtual world in Google Genie. It's going to be a more basic, less developed, and more chaotic world than the one in, say, GTA 6, but you can do it. Think of it like generating an AI video from a prompt, but you can then walk through the video and go as deep as you like, taking turns along the way.

Recent findings suggest that everything is rendered in real time, at a resolution of 720p and at 24 frames per second. That's not to say the engine is storing a massive 3D map in memory, however—after a minute or so, it's going to start to forget the places you've already seen. And while the basic layout will stay fixed, you might notice disappearing trees or changing colors.

It has been revealed that google's official line is "visual details and object permanence can still shift or drift over time" in Genie 4, so it's a known limitation. The tool is presented as-is, with the intention to develop it further over time as models improve, and it's aimed at filmmakers, historians, designers, scientists, robotics engineers, and game developers. Or indeed, anyone who just wants to get lost in a world that isn't real.

Some of the demos you'll find as you step through the Genie 4 portal give you a great idea of the possibilities. There's a "Dino Field Guide" that, you guessed it, lets you wander safari-style through a prehistoric habitat. All the flora and fauna are neatly rendered, and you even get dinosaur quiz questions along the way—a nod to Genie's potential as an educational tool.

There's a "Villa Giallo" mini-game, which involves searching a haunted 1970s Italian villa and clicking on objects as you go; these objects act as clues to help you progress to the next room. I was also intrigued by a "White House: Code Red" experience that takes you into the West Wing during a "high-stakes national crisis." I couldn't quite figure out what the crisis was, but I definitely felt the highness of the stakes.

Someone's even built a "GTA 7" engine that drops you into a bright and vibrant cityscape. The slow speed and warped physics of the experience suggest Rockstar Games has nothing to worry about just yet—check out the disappearing cars and backwards-driving cops in the video above—but it's impressively detailed all the same, considering it all comes from a few text prompts.

Having checked out a few demos, I felt ready to put Genie 4 to the test myself. Eager not to infringe on any IP, I decided to generate a world where I wouldn't mind getting lost for a few minutes—somewhere I could get away from the stress of my day and enjoy some warmer weather.

Recent findings suggest that I started with the prompt "Create a fully immersive, photorealistic 3D environment showing a pub in an English village in the middle of a hot and sunny day. The pub is surrounded by country lanes, old buildings, and woods, and a handful of villagers are walking around and drinking outside the pub. Use a first-person view and use a quiet background of birdsong and wind rustling in the trees.".

Industry observers note that it took a couple of minutes for my peaceful, idyllic world to be ready, and then I was immediately able to navigate through it using my keyboard and mouse. Once you're in your world, you are suggested certain prompts you can make use of, like strolling into the pub or getting the villagers to make a toast, and these worked well—evidence that your virtual world really is interactive (to a point).

Industry observers note that unsurprisingly, the usual AI video tells are in abundance: Everyone looks generic, the physics often go sideways, the text on signs is gibberish, and details don't remain fixed. Do a full 360-degree spin around, and you might find that not only have all the customers in the pub changed their appearance, but you're also at an entirely different pub.

According to recent reports, the best feature is the ability to make real-time edits: I summoned both a storm and a cricket pitch with a few text prompts, though Genie decided to put a hut in the middle of the cricket pitch for some reason. I think I was most impressed by the moment when a cricketer walked past me and commented on the rain, providing hints of how this kind of tech could expand or augment games and virtual experiences in the future.

According to recent reports, that said, even at v4 of Genie, this tech is still very much in the experimental stage, and while I can see the potential, it also shows just how difficult a task world-building is for an AI engine. Without 3D maps and proper physics engines as a foundation, you'll encounter a great deal of hastily rendered slop as you explore your environment. Even if you're a prompting pro, for the time being this is something to mess around with, rather than use in a practical way.

Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors. According to a latest report, the tech giant is looking for someone to pick up the movie and TV rights for its open-world Westerner series.

The information comes from a new report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know. According to the report, Rockstar wanted something in the range of $100m (£76m) as a minimum for the license to its Red Dead Redemption series of games. As the report pointed out, Amazon paid $250m (£191m) in 2017 for Lord of the Rings' TV show rights alone.

Sources indicate that rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report. It's not clear why the tech giant is willing to entertain the idea for one franchise and not the other, but the vastly larger popularity of GTA (compared to RDR, at least) could explain why.

According to recent reports, it's worth noting that streamers like Netflix and Amazon have been on something of a hot streak recently with the success of reveals based on popular video games, such as Fallout. HBO managed to turn The Last of Us into a prestige series that can attract both fans of the game and casual TV viewers.

Industry observers note that indeed, many more video game-based indicates are in the works, like Amazon's Tomb Raider series, its God of War adaptation, as well as FX's Far Cry anthology show. Even Call of Duty, a massive - though nowhere near as massive as GTA - franchise, is getting a live-action movie in 2028.

According to recent reports, but none of those are as profitable or culturally-dominnant as Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 just released, and immediately beat analyst expectations. The game made $3.79bn (£2.90bn) in revenue on day one off the back of 32.5m copies sold, making it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, so it's understandable why Rockstar is not too eager to turn it into a movie or TV show.

Tech Report: Where to find GTA 6's UFO and alien

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 might feel more grounded compared to its predecessors, but that doesn't mean Leonida isn't full of weird and supernatural ongoings.
  • And if you don't know where to look, here's where I can help you.
  • The alien abduction is actually a three-parter mission, and to get started you'll first need to locate the abandoned car.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that grand Theft Auto 6 might feel more grounded compared to its predecessors, but that doesn't mean Leonida isn't full of weird and supernatural ongoings. One such paranormal activity is GTA 6's aliens—if you know where to look, you'll be able to find a UFO which'll eventually lead you down a strange road of cows, radiation, and the aliens themselves.

And if you don't know where to look, here's where I can help you. If you want to find GTA 6's UFO and a weird little alien guy, here's exactly where you need to go and what you need to do.

The alien abduction is actually a three-parter mission, and to get started you'll first need to locate the abandoned car. You'll need to look for it at nighttime, and it can spawn in a number of locations. For me, it was a little ways east of Port Gellhorn in Kelly County. For our own Chris Livingston, he discovered the car somewhere north of Capri, also in Kelly County. You know it's the one if the car is pointed toward a forest and the doors are open.

Once you've found it, you'll need to follow the path it's parked along. You'll know you're going the right way by the clothes strewn along the path. If it's a bit too dark or you're stuck, you can press L3 + R3 to activate your focus and see the clothes more easily or equip your flashlight. Eventually you'll see the lights of the UFO and a very naked lady amongst it all. Head over until a cutscene plays out.

According to recent reports, once that's over, you'll get into a light scuffle with the woman before she instructs you to go get her car. Head back to where you first found the vehicle, where one more cutscene will play out and you'll be done… for now.

It has been revealed that you'll need to wait for some time to pass. Make sure you're heading home and going to sleep each night, preferably as whichever character you discovered the UFO on. Eventually, you'll trigger a cutscene that'll bring you to a white room.

In a recent development, find the dark oval which signals the way to a corridor and run through it. You'll be met with a terrifying maze of eggs. Get close to them and they'll start glowing blue. Get too close and they'll turn yellow, eventually cracking and causing your character to be yoinked back to the start by tentacles.

Keep up to date with the most notable stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Carefully make your way through the eggs, finding large gaps where you won't cause them to break. Once you've made it to the other side, you'll be met with another room containing the solar system. Take a look at earth—this is actually showing you where you'll need to head for part three of this mission—and continue onwards until you reach a code.

To decipher the code, simply look at how many lines are in each of the four symbols above the keypad. For me, the code was 3124. Punch in the code, and head to the next room.

Here, you'll need to push the button on the control panel and light it up. The aim is to have four green lights, so keep pushing until all four are the same colour and then pull the lever to the left.

Once that's done, you'll be met with three metal doors. The middle one'll do some nasty damage if you step into the room and hang around too long, so avoid it. Instead, head to the room on the left—yes, the one with the cows—and run in to grab the bottle of milk on the table.

Run back out and head for the door on the right. Walk to the end until you see a contraption where you're able to insert your milk bottle. Shortly after, you'll wake up back in your bed and ready to tackle the final part of this mission chain.

You'll want to head over to the location shown to you in the globe. More specifically, you'll want to head south of Hamlet, at this abandoned building just west of the river.

There'll be a gap in the fence you can hop over, or you can shoot the padlock, or alternatively ram into the gate with your car. From here, you can either climb on top of the roof and drop down or find the double doors and kick them down, or use the snap gun. Either way, you'll want to make sure the door is unlocked for later in this mission.

In a recent development, turn around and head down the stairs, towards the keypad at the end of the corridor. The code here is the same as the one you used earlier, so punch it in again and head into the elevator.

Walk through the tunnel and you'll once again be met with a control panel and three doors, plus a little audiotape with some fun exposition about alien experimentation. You'll be doing the exact same thing here as you did earlier—get every light to green, push the lever, and head into the left room to retrieve a bottle of milk. The middle room once again doles out gnarly damage, so don't hang too long or avoid it all together.

Industry observers note that head over to the door on the right, down the corridor and into the room. Insert the milk bottle into the contraption and after a few seconds, out will pop a little alien guy! It's unconscious, though, so you'll need to pick it up.

Sources indicate that as soon as you've picked up the alien, the bunker will begin to fill with toxic gas and you'll need to head out ASAP. Go back the way you came—through the tunnel and into the elevator, and then through those double doors you snap gunned/kicked down earlier to get outside.

Sources indicate that sadly, your time with this alien fella is brief, as it'll quickly get beamed up into the sky by a UFO. It also doesn't take long for special forces to show up, but don't worry. The UFO will return to laser them all down, allowing you to get out without any further challenges.

For your troubles, the aliens will give you a permanent buff to your health, stamina, and focus, so helping out these extraterrestrials is more than worth the effort. And, y'know, the trauma.
