It has been revealed that in as booming a monster truck rally commentator voice as you can imagine: ARE YOU READY TO GET DECIMATED??? Yes? Yippee! Because I've got some good news for you. The latest enhancement for Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 is here, appropriately dubbed the Decimation update, which adds in a upcoming mode and more.

First up, that new mode! It's called Weekly Clash and it's for the competitive folks out there. "This new PvP shakes things up with the introduction of “Weekly Clash”, a new mode that brings unique new rules to Eternal War, like games restricted to a single class, a single weapon or even granting near-unlimited grenades," explains a Steam blog post. "Except more modifiers to be added in the future.".

This update also introduces a new Chaos Siege sector, that new mode introduced last month, which adds in a "new playable sector bringing a renewed challenge between waves 11 and 15!" You'll also find six new heroic weapons in the armoury, like the omnissian axe, plasma incinerator and heavy bolter. This comes complete with some new heroic armour pieces, specifically four new helmets. On top of all of this, there's been a Vanguard rework: "Fight the enemies of Humanity with new ways to use your Grapnel Launcher! Attack cancellations, close-quarter kicks and a new Revenge mechanic make the Vanguard as bold and brutal as he’s ever been!".

Some other general tweaks have been made with this patch too. All PvP maps have seen the number and locations of ammo and equipment pickups adjusted, and conditions for the spawn position swap system have been improved. A level lock for the Absolute Siege and Absolute Stratagems mode has also been added; "The difficulty will be accessible to Classes that have reached level 25 or achieved Prestige at least once." And you'll also find that loading times and general connectivity should be a bit better!

  • It has been revealed that the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.

In a recent development, after infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.

It has been revealed that the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.

Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository.

Sources indicate that "I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.

"Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've remarked before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC. The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but rapidly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.

It has been revealed that incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.

Industry observers note that rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the organization has not revealed GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, earlier than everyone expected.

If you're among the millions already playing the game on consoles, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough contains a wealth of information covering all major mechanics, main missions, secrets, cheats and more besides.

Tidal Is the First Streaming Platform to Ban AI Music

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that you have a few options when it comes to choosing a music streaming service.
  • It has been revealed that on Tuesday, Tidal confirmed intends to ban AI music from its platform entirely.
  • This isn't the first stand Tidal has taken against AI-generated music.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that you have a few options when it comes to choosing a music streaming service. If you own an iPhone and a Mac, you might be tempted by Apple Music; if you have more friends on Spotify, you may feel that's the best platform for you. But if your goal is avoiding AI music as much as humanly possible, there appears to be a newly introduced uncontested winner: Tidal.

It has been revealed that on Tuesday, Tidal confirmed intends to ban AI music from its platform entirely. Starting Dec. 9, the firm will begin taking steps to remove music it believes is entirely made with AI. Tidal states it thinks the move “will resonate with both artists and listeners alike.”.

This isn't the first stand Tidal has taken against AI-generated music. Back in July, the manufacturer announced that it would start labeling songs completely made with AI, as well as remove tracks it found to be "fraudulent and deceptive." Other platforms have similar policies, or are rolling out similar features. Apple Music, for example, is working on AI labels for its app, too, and Spotify has pushed back on AI to some degree. However, this most recent move makes Tidal the first music streaming service to outright ban AI-generated music from its catalog.

Recent findings suggest that robert Anderson, Tidal's Music Lead, posted on X about the change. According to Anderson, Tidal identified 43% of the tracks it received in the last 90 days were AI-generated. Per the company's strategy, Tidal will remove 29 million songs by the beginning of 2027, roughly 80,000 to 85,000 removals per day. Some 96% of Tidal's AI-generated songs have zero plays whatsoever.

Industry observers note that I wouldn't be surprised to see other music streaming services follow suit, particularly Apple Music. Despite rolling out AI-powered features over the past couple of years, including Apple Music's AI-generated playlists, Apple has taken some stands against AI-generated material in general. The latest Apple TV intro was shot in-camera with practical effects, in an era where the firm could have easily generated something with AI. If other companies plan to follow Tidal's lead here, my money's on Apple being first in line.

However, as it stands, Tidal is the only streaming service that supports this initiative. Soon enough, it'll be the sole music app you can use with near-zero ambiguity that the music you're listening to was at least mostly created by humans. (What a sentence.) Avoiding AI-generated music can be tricky, frustrating, and, frankly, exhausting. If that's important to you, Tidal might just be your latest pick.

There really isn't much I need in life, but that certainly fulfills those needs. And it's exactly what HARK THE GHOUL is offering, an action-adventure, dungeon crawler RPG set in a weird and nasty Victorian gothic city with an emphasis on free exploration.

Now, I appreciate not all of you will be as immediately convinced by trench coat wearing rat men, so let's have a deeper gander at the game together. Exploration really does seem to be the key thing here, not just in terms of going wherever you want, more or less when you want, but how you get about. For example, say there's an annoying gap you want to cross. Use a magical spell to summon a crate, then lob it in front of you, and cast some icey magic to freeze it into place, thereby creating a upcoming platform for you to hop onto. Looks like nice and systemic stuff!

HARK THE GHOUL releases 👉JANUARY 21st, 2027!!!👈 Our action-adventure RPG built around freeform exploration lets you loose in a dark Victorian city full of secrets to uncover and ravenous monsters to defeat! Coming to Steam, Switch 1, Switch 2, PS5 and Xbox Series![image or embed].

Industry observers note that this extends to the combat, which faces you against odd automatons, infected foes and nasty beasties. You can perform quite silly tricks like using your shovel to dig up a rock and chuck that at a baddie, or you can use your magic to conjure up an explosive crate which you then kick at an enemy, blasting it with a shotgun. It appears to almost be an RPG by way of the immersive sim; there's no correct way to go about the game, only the way you find most fun. Though maybe that's dredging up the debate around what an immersive sim is….

Sources indicate that either way, I'm just tickled pink by HARK THE GHOUL, which also pits you as a mothman-type figure who's just emerged from their cocoon. Delightful! And it just got a release date too: January 21st, 2027. That's only a couple of months away, obviously, but if you can't wait that long then there's a demo you can check out on Steam. Or, you know, just throw it a wishlist! Offering it some support either way seems like a nice idea.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as people have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.

According to recent reports, this new option arrived fairly quietly as part of an upgrade that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup. That addition may have generated the most headlines, but it's this one little toggle that's getting many players exicted.

According to recent reports, why is this such a significant deal? Previously, the bordered image on the 4:3 aspect ratio games contained lots of little dots, and players complained that these were distracting at best, and casused discomfort on the eyes whilst playing at worst. Other players worried it would contribute to screen burn-in on older televsion sets. As part of the new patch, you can simply border your games with plain black - a tiny revision, but one that you can already see online communities celebrating. The player icon (another UI element that attracts derision) is still present, however, but as one comment summarises: "it's a step in the right direction".

It has been revealed that "Oh my gawd, I've been wanting this! I hate the checkered on the side, it clashed with every game I tried," says one social media user." Players have been complaining about these borders and UI elements since Nintendo Classics was introduced on the Nintendo Switch back on 18th September, 2018. So it's taken a good eight years for Nintendo to - finally - implement a change.

According to recent reports, in order to change the border yourself, you need to head to the game library selection screen on the Nintendo Classics app, navigate to the game settings, and locate the option to toggle this border graphic in the "Extra Elements Display" tab. Hit the button and - bang - you're done. At the time of writing, this option only appears on the GameCue app, and only on Switch 2, but people on social media are already asking Nintendo to enable it across the original Switch and other apps in the library, too.

Industry observers note that not everyone is happy with the 'slowly, slowly' approach Nintendo is taking towards implementing these changes, though. "Why can't we expect the full step with no graphic at all?" asks one irritated poster on Reddit. "Why do you have to deal with these half assed implementations for a paid deluxe subscription service?".

"Oh well, probably gotta wait another 10 years for the next improvement" says another. Another slightly more constructive user outlines what helpful additons might look like, noting that adding a "blurred zoomed in image of the game to fill out the background, or just extending the colors outward into the border, or maybe something fun like a CRT TV-looking border like the NES and SNES Classic had" would go a long way to make the retro experience better on the consoles.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One thing I think that’s really underrated about Hallmark is how the network’s projects manage to do a lot without the world’s largest budgets. (These aren't upcoming MCU movies!) Sometimes, however, a little bit of good karma wafts a production’s way just like a snowflake in the crisp winter air. This is exactly what happened on the set of Mistletoe Murders when the show found Fletcher’s Grove, the cool small town hide out Emily Lane (Sarah Drew) opens her Christmas shop in. Apparently, the show has Reacher to thank for this.

While Reacher is not known for having the insane budgets some of Amazon Prime Videos other reveals like Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power have had, the show did once create an entire facade for a small town and then left it behind after less than a month.

If you’ve seen Reacher, you know the set. It’s on the Pickering Backlot in Ontario, and it was used during Season 1 to create Margrave, the fictional Georgia town that sees Jack Reacher facing the death of his brother and getting accused of murder himself. It’s a great season of TV, and it came with a pretty nice set, so nice that when Mistletoe Murders was scouting around, they thought it would be the perfect setting for Fletcher’s Grove.

Hallmark brought CinemaBlend to the set of Mistletoe Murders, where producer Michelle Melanson told me what happened, and how they fortuitously came across the former Reacher property.

I believe they used it for 18 shoot days. That’s it. And then they left it. It’s on land owned by the city of Pickering, but William F. White at Sunbelt said, ‘Well we can maybe use this, we can rent it to productions.’ So, that’s what they did, they sort of rented it to productions. And when we saw it – it’s a little small town – we were like, ‘This is Fletcher’s Grove.’.

To Amazon’s credit, there’s a little more to it than just having an excess of money to build a whole city and dump it. Season 1 of Reacher was originally expected to film in Georgia. Then, the pandemic hit and prepares changed. It was easier and safer to build a little town on a spot in the middle of nowhere in Canada, and that’s exactly what the show did.

Sources indicate that now, it’s a bit of “backlot trivia” in Mistletoe Murders’ own story, though the Hallmark series also has its own indoor set, which helps them to control temperature while filming during hot summers. It also gives them the ability to move forward should Amazon ever want to tear down the “real” Margrave/Fletcher’s Grove.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

So that’s our little backlot trivia. We dress it up. That’s where the Mistletoe is. This year we’re excited; we have things like a Christmas market. We wanted to save ourselves because this backlot could go away at any time. They could decide they don’t want to keep it; so we built this set.

It has been revealed that I love it when two indicates I deeply enjoy have synergy like this. Prior to being able to visit the set of Mistletoe Murders ahead of this fall's Season 3 return on the 2026 TV schedule, I would never have known the Sarah Drew-led series would have anything in common with the Alan Ritchson series, but this is one very cool connection.

According to recent reports, pinball remains such an intoxicating game because it's one where you have to constantly be on your toes. As the tiny metal sphere bats about the place, it's down to you to hit it at just the right time so as to keep racking up points upon points. It's a game of skill as much as it is luck. It is also incredibly silly, which is why I'm so tickled by Appulse, a sci-fi pinball roguelite top-down shooter that introduced today wherein your ball is actually the main defence system on your spaceship.

Yes! This is also silly! Especially considering the semi-realistic sci-fi vibe of it all. It encourages me to wonder who in this world looked at pinball and thought, "yes, this is the optimum method of defending our ship from invading robots." And I love this fictional character for such a thought!

Industry observers note that at its most basic function, Appulse works exactly as you'd expect from a pinball game, in that you shoot your ball, or ship in this case, and hit those flappers to keep it in the air, so to speak. Accept the key difference is your ball/ship has guns that you use to shoot the aforementioned invading robots, while also doubling up as an extra method for control. Need to right a bad hit? Shoot your shot and you'll fly off in the opposite direction.

I've seen this in other digital pinball games before, but that's not a knock, I can't imagine having to manage all this shooting without some semblance of control. The roguelite mechanics sound pretty nifty too. You can get perks like extra recoil when firing, which obviously will aid you in staying in control. Or you may unlock the ability to slow down time. Builds sound pretty flexible! And overall it just looks like a neat little time. If Appulse takes your fancy, then as mentioned it's available to pick up on Steam now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, yellowjackets, the time-hopping survival drama about a group of teenage girls who are stranded in the wilderness in 1996 and do terrible things to survive, is coming to an end. Whether or not it sticks the landing, it's been one helluva ride, and we'll soon have room in the streaming schedule for other other indicates about young people having a pretty rough go of it while just trying to survive.

Sources indicate that situated between flashbacks and flash-forwards (not entirely unlike Yellowjackets), mystery/thriller The Wilds sees an airplane full of teenage girls crash on the way to an empowerment program in Hawaii. It rapidly becomes clear that the accident was engineered and that the whole thing is some sort of social experiment, and the survivors are forced to compete against each other if they want to live. The show understands the ways in which young women are exploited and expected to compete against each other in the real world, not just a show about girlfights. Stream The Wilds on Prime Video.

A bit more grounded...but only at first glance, The Stranded takes place on a Thai island in the midst of a tsunami. The island was formerly home to a prestigious high school, and a bunch of students have snuck back for an ill-timed party on the last day of class. A bad idea, clearly, after the storm hits. Kraam (Papangkorn Lerkchaleampote), one of the few students who actually lives on the island, is trapped there along with a couple dozen classmates. Kraam knows the island, but Anan (Chutavuth Pattarakampol) assumes leadership while other students either take on necessary roles or fall in line. As the miniseries progresses, the new social order breaks down, even as the island's mysteries reveal themselves and things get weirder and more complex. Stream The Stranded on Netflix.

Sources indicate that A handful of influencers get invited to a remote island, which is obviously a very good thing to agree to that will not lead to dramatic complications in any way. Behind the neon-lit party vibes, there's a cult at work and some ritualistic shenanigans with deadly consequences. Eden is more concerned with the survival horror than with some of the deeper themes and mysteries of Yellowjackets, but we're still playing with shifting power dynamics in this Spanish import. Stream Welcome to Eden on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that the premise of The Leftovers is brilliantly subdued: Around two percent of the world's population disappears without explanation, and it's enough to upend just about everything. Politics have adapted to the new normal, religions have collapsed and reformed, and families have had to make peace with the inexplicable loss of loved ones. The first season revolves around the Garvey family, led by Kevin (Justin Theroux), a sheriff whose wife (Amy Brenneman) left him to join a cult, while subsequent seasons broaden the scope to bring in other characters in other locations. It's more philosophical than Yellowjackets, and quieter, but the shows share an interest in the lingering effects of trauma, and in the stuff we get up to under threat and in the dark. Stream The Leftovers on HBO Max.

Recent findings suggest that the 100 tells the story of the descendants of refugees of nuclear devastation who return to Earth from their habitat in space to encounter the remnants of humanity who have survived on Earth. Naturally, the first people sent to scope things out are the juvenile delinquents (better them than me), and they discover that three civilizations have risen up in the aftermath of the apocalypse, and they are all pretty scary (including one populated by cannibals, naturally). More sci-fi than horror, but the survivalist themes and mysteries here make it more than a decent match. The show builds an impressive mythology over the course of its run, leading to a conclusion that’s borderline metaphysical. Stream The 100 on Pluto TV or buy it from Prime Video.

Sources indicate that when pretty, popular girl Kate Wallis (Olivia Holt) goes missing without a trace in 1993, awkward Jeanette Turner (Chiara Aurelia) steps in to fill the gap, modeling herself after Kate by working her way into the missing girl's social circle and getting close with her boyfriend. That's all going great until Kate reappears two years later, accusing Jeanette of having witnessed the events around her disappearance and keeping quiet. Whoops. There's even more going on, as the show shifts back and forth between 1993, 1994, and 1995 to slowly reveal the missing pieces. Season two takes on a different story set in 1999 and 2000, and the forthcoming (surprise) third season will shake things up again. The emphasis here is on mystery, but it's a show about the aftereffects of trauma and of the dark secrets that can tear families and communities apart. Stream Cruel Summer on Hulu.

It has been revealed that A massive apocalyptic tidal wave strikes during the 10-year reunion of the graduating class of an all-girls high school. The event leaves them all trapped together (a nightmare in any event), and forced to survive while reliving old struggles and dramas. It's Yellowjackets-esque, absolutely, but also Australian and a comedy, which doesn't feel like as much of a stretch as you'd think given the over-the-top nature of that show. Stream Class of '07 on Prime Video.

A remote, charming town with some deep, dark secrets (the biggest of which, and one that it shares with Yellowjackets, is rather strongly hinted in the title), Gannibal stars Yuya Yagira as Daigo Agawa, a police officer from the big city who takes a job in the super cute (and, of course, remote) village of Kuge following some personal trouble. The perfectly charming Goto family runs the town, more or less, and welcomes Daigo and his family. It's all looking pretty great—until a mysterious man gives Daigo's daughter a severed finger as a gift, and his wife Yuki finds the words "Run Away" scrawled over a door in their newly introduced home. Just a couple of reasons why I'm more of a city person. Stream Gannibal on Disney+ and Hulu.

Recent findings suggest that this latter-day plane crash narrative goes all-in on mystery and philosophy, virtually pioneering the timey-wimey reveal format that makes Yellowjackets so juicy. We kick off with flashbacks that peel back the layers of the various crash survivors before diving headfirst into warm-weather polar bears and mysterious underground bunkers and monsters made of smoke. Whether it's an uncommonly smart network show that rewards careful viewing or a load of nonsense is in the eye of the beholder—but it remains one of the most discussed and debated indicates in TV history. Stream Lost on Disney+ and Hulu.

Kathryn Newton heads this surprisingly smart Lord of the Flies riff about a group of teenagers forced to create their own community after all the adults disappear and a dense fresh forest crops up around their small enclave, cutting them off from everything and everyone else. This one's about coming of age in a world where the usual rules are no longer in effect, and about how we're quick to reestablish an oppressive social order even when outside forces are no longer at work. Stream The Society on Netflix.

As Blizzard whacks one World of Warcraft: Forever gold farming exploit, it struggles to contain all of the alternatives popping up

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever is in the grip of a gold-farming bonanza, as Blizzard's attempts to curb them are met with a seemingly endless wave of alternative money-making methods.
  • Sources indicate that first, some context.
  • For one, it was the first time Blizzard has put a stop to a specific money-making strategy in Forever.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever is in the grip of a gold-farming bonanza, as Blizzard's attempts to curb them are met with a seemingly endless wave of alternative money-making methods.

Sources indicate that first, some context. Last week an exploitative method of making gold in the game was removed. The exploit involved repeatedly running the upcoming Blackmaw Hold dungeon and rapidly killing non-elite enemies which were - mistakenly - given better loot drops than they were supposed to have. This was taken out, and people exploiting this to extreme degrees were temporarily suspended and had trading blocks put on their accounts. In addition, gold gained this way was removed from their accounts.

This was a big deal. For one, it was the first time Blizzard has put a stop to a specific money-making strategy in Forever. But in the days following Blizzard's action, other exploits have been discovered requiring similar action.

Sources indicate that let's start with dungeon farming. In World of Warcraft, you are limited to entering 10 separate dungeon instances per hour before the game starts locking you out. This farming method is based around promptly entering these dungeons, killing the mobs for loot, leaving and resetting the dungeon, then rinsing and repeating. Do this 10 times and you've got a handsome payday.

Some players were running into the side entrance of the Uldaman dungeon to kill a specific boss, The Obsidian Sentinel, in a way that would take just a few minutes. So people were able to farm valuable boss loot and max the dungeon limit of 20-30 gold earned in an hour. This exploit has been killed, with Blizzard removing the loot from this boss to temporarily curb the strategy.

Industry observers note that this isn't without its complications. Primarily, by removing the loot from that aforementioned Uldaman boss, several strong items had been removed for regular players. This included one part of the beloved Pendulum of Doom axe, which was unobtainable in-game until the loot was turned back on for the boss.

It has been revealed that however, this is far from the only dungeon farming method. Players are now repeatedly farming non-boss enemies in the latest Krol'dok Stronghold to earn potentially upwards of 100 gold an hour. And presumably more people are looking for more exploits all the time. Blizzard, in turn, has had to halve the instance cap in World of Warcraft: Forever to five to attempt to get control of the situation.

So that's the end of it, right? Well, no! While these instanced farms have proven lucrative, they are far from the only way of gathering vast amounts of gold. Already, players have discovered that by grouping and killing Furbolgs in Felwood, they can all pick up beads - seemingly another bug in the game. These can be exchanged for items, which in turn can be sold off to a vendor for a tidy profit.

In a recent development, even if this gets patched, there are other 'valid' farms capable of turning a quick profit. You can, for example, kill turtles in Mount Hyjal and skin them for valuable leather and turtle scales, not to mention their meat and occasional trash to sell to vendors. Why is this valid while dungeon farms aren't? It raises the question: what makes a gold-farming method worth fixing?

In a recent development, it's a tricky problem. To defend gold farmers for a moment, the game has a history of gold farming that has been permitted. For years, mages have been blasting down dungeon mobs without fear of ban nor suspension. In response to the Blackmaw Hold fix, Blizzard remarked: "Finding efficient farming spots has always been a part of the game, and is how most players have earned their epic mounts since 2004. When a single location proves so lucrative that it overshadows all other sources, we generally adjust it to bring it in line with the rest.".

Sources indicate that so the line appears to be the level of profit made from a particular farm. Though without this line being drawn explicitly, one wonders how gold farmers will know whether their strategy is safe or not. There is a culture around goldfarming that has existed since the game first released in the early 2000s. These aren't bad players. They aren't even naughty players, really. They've been a part of the game's culture for over 20 years.

At the same time, it's hard not to feel for the developers here. This is not the same World of Warcraft as the one players jumped into decades ago. Long gone are the days when a few guildies could accrue wealth with a humble farming method. Gold farmers are now equipped with the skills to efficiently harvest mobs with ease, and can quickly hop between server layers to access mobs quicker, and when a lucrative farm is found, it can be kept secret within Discord servers and run endlessly until Blizzard wisens up.

It has been revealed that at the same time, the developers have to stay on top of this stuff. Already the in-game economy is getting more expensive as time goes on, and those who have taken their time to level with friends are facing fiscal pressures that those who rushed through it did not encounter. All the while, Blizzard has acknowledged that gold farming is a part of the game, and so the pressure not to cater to some good ol' fashioned hustling is doubtless weighing on their shoulders.

In a recent development, what will likely happen is this. Gold farmers will bounce around with the developers hot on their tails until finally the farms deemed unintended or exploitative are made untenable. That's when and where the line will be drawn. This will likely be a continuous problem as updates bring more potential money-making opportunities to the game, but it's safe to say there's an element of uncertainty surrounding the situation.

Industry observers note that the big question is whether the events of the Blackmaw Hold suspensions put enough fear into the hearts of gold farmers to curb their exploitative habits? If it hasn't, do the developers have the nerve to dish out more severe punishments? Time, as always, will be the test of it.

Sources indicate that for those of you who aren't already max level and farming gold, or trapped up in Winterspring, grinding out Wintersaber Trainers reputation for no reason (me), it's worth emphasising that World of Warcraft: Forever does bring a lot of the magic of the original game back alongside quality of life changes. Give it a go, if you dare.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director.
  • It has been revealed that "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, indicates in an interview with Eurogamer.
  • The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 doesn't just mark a huge, and at times unbelievable, step forward for graphics; it's also at the forefront of what an open world game can be, just look at the existential crisis it's given Cyberpunk 2's creative director. With thousands of enterable buildings, unpredictable and slightly scary NPCs, and systems that help you determine what kind of criminal you want to be. It all really does feel like a milestone for what videogames can do.

It has been revealed that "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics," Rob Nelson, Rockstar's head of development, indicates in an interview with Eurogamer. "So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun.".

The sophisticated mechanics that Nelson is talking about here pertains to GTA 6's Criminal Profile, a system that evaluates your escapades across Leonida and gives you a rating. There's Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho, and Irredeemable. The more stealthy and non-lethal you are, the higher your profile will be. It's similar to Red Dead Redemption 2's Honor System.

According to recent reports, "There was maybe more emotional resonance in the story of RDR2 than we had, certainly in a GTA before," Nelson states. "So we liked that idea. We didn't necessarily come to GTA 6 going: 'We must have emotional resonance,' but all of those things combine. It's more that those systems and that element of player choice and agency, and the way that affected the narrative, was a hard thing to ignore and walk away from.".

Nelson explains that most of the groundwork started as "simple things" in principle, "but they create a lot more work in terms of development of the sophistication of the systems." It's all about choice in GTA 6. You choose whether you want to be a criminal with a conscience or a loose cannon.

"It's still a world of violence, but you could threaten somebody by aiming a gun at them and just robbing them, and they have a chance to comply. So you don't have to beat them to death to get their money.".

The part that sticks out the most is that you "don't have to" approach crimes in a certain way, there's still the option to go into every encounter guns blazing because redemption only works from a storytelling perspective when it's the player's choice, and not as Nelson puts it, something that is "foisted upon you".

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

According to recent reports, "You can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks," Nelson adds. "And then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically notes, 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'".

In a recent development, am I brave enough to reject the criminal profile system entirely? Hell no. I replay sections of dialogue if I accidentally upset someone, and cannot do an "evil run" of a game without giving myself stomach ulcers because of the guilt—but I appreciate having the option.

In a recent development, so how has that relationship been? According to Remedy CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon, working with Rockstar has been "amazing". "Honestly, it's been great," Gaudechon told Game File. "You know why? Because I think they're super respectful of Remedy.".

Gaudechon is so positive on Remedy's working relationship with Rockstar that he emphasised his praise for Rockstar further. "I'll say it out loud: They've honestly been an awesome partner. And it's no bullshit," he added.

In a recent development, the original Max Payne was released in 2001, and its sequel in 2003 - both developed by Remedy. Rockstar published the second game and worked on the original's console ports. Rockstar developed a third entry in the series, Max Payne 3, which Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser recently called something of a failure.

Industry observers note that "Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success," noted Houser.

Industry observers note that the Max Payne 1 & 2 remake has been in the works since 2022, but only entered full production in 2024. The game is understood to be Remedy's current project, though the studio also has another unannounced project in the works.

In a recent development, maths is not my strong suit, I make no secret of this, so when I come face to face with something like sudoku I will admit to recoiling in fear at having to confront this problem. Numbers don't make sense to me at the best of times, and now I have to figure out the specific placements of them whereby each number can only be used once per section, and each column and row have to all contain numbers one through nine? Terrifying! No, thanks, I'd much rather do the exact same thing but with, I don't know, skeletons and ghouls and the like. Which, conveniently, is more or less what Dungoku offers, a genre mashup of dungeon crawling and sudoku with a retro dark fantasy vibe.

In a recent development, okay, it's not exactly the same. You don't crawl the dungeons in the typical fashion here as it leans heavily towards the puzzle side of things. Maps come in different, grid-based shapes and sizes, but to start they are mostly void of enemies. It's predominantly up to you to place enemies, or sometimes chests, in specific squares, all of which have their own rules that you must follow, with a set number that need to be placed on the map.

For example, one enemy may have a requirement that it is adjacent to a zombie in the same room. Another might need to be placed in a dead end. Others, like an owl creature, can only share a room with itself or other animals. So, it's different from sudoku in that each puzzle features changing enemies that have to be placed, as opposed to always needing to follow the same basic rules. It seems like a clever spin on the classic puzzle! Plus there's loot to be acquired that improves your stats and thereby your chance of survival (making a mistake in placement results in, obviously, getting hurt; this is still a dungeon crawler!).

Industry observers note that in total there's apparently over 100 "hand-crafted dungeons to explore," and more than 20 monsters to take on, so it sounds like there's some good potential for interesting puzzle combinations. I also like the specific mention of "human composed music," certainly makes it sound like AI wasn't involved, and lord almighty I hope that to be true! No release date attached to this one just yet, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

After a lot of fan requests for a remake of The Simpsons: Hit & Run, there were many clues suggesting the project was finally up and running — but now, things don't look so certain.

As reported by VGC, Darren Evenson — who was a senior game designer at Newly introduced Radical Games, the team thought to be producing the Hit & Run revival — has posted on LinkedIn about projects being cancelled at the studio.

"It seems that not even a fantastic project with an absolutely incredible team is immune from the current state of the industry right now, as what we were working on at Fresh Radical Games (although mind-blowingly awesome) was part of a whole gaggle of cancellations," Evenson notes.

Industry observers note that "Oh, you silly suits with spreadsheets... will you EVER learn? If you don't make the game, you can't make the money... and if you don't make the money, then you don't get the power... and... well, there's more to that quote, but I digress.

For the first time in my career, I am Available For Work and looking for a new exciting opportunity where I can make some fun games with some great people!

Please reach out, shout out, or peform some interpretive dance if you know of an opportunity that a hip cat like me could groove to.".

Fans who have spotted this message are fairly confident, based on certain quotes, that it's referring to The Simpsons: Hit & Run, though others have suggested it could actually be Scarface: The World Is Yours.

New Radical Games is a recently founded studio with many key staff from Radical Entertainment, the Canadian outfit that made the original Hit & Run.

Between that and the show's creator, Matt Groening, practically confirming the remake's existence, it was thought that it was finally going to happen.

While this new message doesn't outright say the remake is cancelled, something has been, and Hit & Run was the most obvious candidate for the studio's main project.

We'll have to wait and see how things play out, but for now, it feels like the elusive remake may not be so close as we thought, and may in fact not be coming at all.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, EA wanted a World of Warcraft killer when it bought BioWare in 2007, according to Dragon Age producer Mark Darrah. But he claims BioWare's MMO, Star Wars: The Old Republic, never did WoW numbers, and EA's higher-ups always "hated" it as a result.

In a recent development, bioWare was first acquired in 2005 by a private equity fund alongside Pandemic Studios, makers of the original Star Wars: Battlefront games, and packaged under a single holding tech giant. While Darrah notes that he was a programmer in this era, and thus didn't have a great insight into BioWare's financial situation, his "understanding is that we basically had no money left. We needed money to continue to exist.".

In an interview for podcast Pembridge TV, Darrah explains that BioWare intentionally "made games that were bigger than other people's games," and the studio continued to expand its scope by hiring more people. While the original studio, based in Edmonton, continued to develop single-player RPGs, BioWare opened a newly introduced studio in Austin, Texas to work on the massively multiplayer online game that would become Star Wars: The Old Republic. That, Darrah believes, is the true reason EA acquired BioWare.

Industry observers note that "EA's always wanted everything to be a live service," Darrah notes. "They just didn't use that language in the past. Back in the days before Destiny, the thing that was seen as the successful live service model was the MMO. Everyone wanted an MMO. World of Warcraft came out and totally redefined the space. Everyone wanted a World of Warcraft killer. I mean, it was Star Wars. Surely it could be the World of Warcraft killer.".

So, as part of a package deal with BioWare's single-player RPG studio in Edmonton and Pandemic, EA bought its potential WoW killer. Darrah recalls speculating on why EA was laying out so much money for the acquisition: "It's like, 'okay, well, they really want Star Wars: The Old Republic. They want the MMO. They obviously want [Battlefront].' Then it's like, 'oh, and they're getting BioWare Edmonton.' For me, and for many people in Edmonton at the time of the acquisition, it looked like EA was buying Star Wars: The Old Republic and Pandemic and getting BioWare Edmonton as a side effect.".

Of course, Pandemic ended up being an early casualty of the acquisition, as EA shut it down in 2009. "Star Wars: The Old Republic more than paid for itself eventually, but it took a really long time. The probably single best return on investment that EA got was BioWare Edmonton, even though it seemed like we were just an afterthought.".

But while The Old Republic eventually made back EA's investment the publisher resented the game for failing to meet its lofty expectations at launch.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

"EA hated SWTOR from the beginning," Darrah indicates, pointing particular blame at then-EA studios boss Patrick Söderlund. "They wanted it really bad, but all indication – and someone from Austin could probably speak to this more than me – it always seemed to me like they wanted it gone pretty much from the instant it rolled out and didn't hit its numbers. They never wanted to invest in it. They always wanted to push it out of the conversation. They talked about pulling people off of it for a really long time. But it did generate money.".

Recent findings suggest that still, Darrah suggests that the exact same thing happened when BioWare made its next live-service game, Anthem. By that time, MMOs were looking like old news. "If you're not WoW are going to come out, and then they're going to go free-to- play and then they're going to slowly decay away," Darrah says. But he puts EA's perspective like this: "We don't want that. We want Destiny. Destiny's making so much money.".

Then, of course, Anthem came out, had its moment, and slowly decayed away. The irony is that, at this point, The Old Republic – which is still running and receiving fresh content – is set to outlast Anthem, Destiny, and even BioWare itself.

"Maybe most corporations are incapable of learning those lessons," Darrah laments.

Former Dragon Age lead notes EA mismanagement killed BioWare by forcing it into terrible choices: "They made us do something".

According to recent reports, dustin Bailey joined the GamesRadar team as a Staff Writer in May 2022, and is currently based in Missouri. He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest major action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not.
  • At its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that cupertino is one of those TV highlights that arrived just when we all needed it. In this economy, a story about two lawyers who get shafted by the “move fast and break things” culture of Silicon Valley and decide to use their legal chops to fight back was almost destined to be a hit, and the great performances by Mike Colter and Rachel Keller sealed the deal. If you love the sharp legal wrangling and tech-focused storylines and want a movie that perfectly complements the show, it’s time to watch (or re-watch) Aaron Sorkin and David Fincher’s 2010 masterpiece, The Social Network.

Just like Cupertino, The Social Network arrived at precisely the right moment in history—just when everyone was beginning to wonder if the social media revolution kicked off by Facebook and Mark Zuckerberg was actually a good idea or not. While it might seem hard to imagine, there was a time when Facebook was the social media platform—everyone was on it, and it dominated the conversation like nothing else. And the outsized wealth and influence Zuckerberg accrued as a result were just starting to make people a little uneasy.

At its core, The Social Network is a legal drama—the framing narrative involves dual lawsuits brought against Zuckerberg and the depositions he is giving, which prompt flashbacks to the formation and success of Facebook in the early 2000s. Like Cupertino, the story is soaked in the “apologize later” culture of tech startups, and traces the ruthlessness and cold genius of Zuckerberg as he cements his control over the platform, ices out former partners, and generally behaves like a sociopathic genius (Jesse Eisenberg’s performance as Zuckerberg is coldly compelling).

The film doesn’t have any kind of clear-cut ending where the good guys win, but there’s a certain satisfaction in the way Sorkin’s script and Eisenberg’s performance strip away the glamour of Zuckerberg’s money and success, reducing him in many ways to an aggrieved loner who translated his rage into a brilliant idea, and then has to isolate himself from everyone in order to maintain his control over it. The Zuckerberg depicted in the film is a lonely, bitter dude, and it’s as much of a happy ending as you’ll get. It’s a fascinating story of legal maneuvering and bickering lawyers against a backdrop of one of the foundational social media moments that shaped modern culture, and fans of the show will dig it. Stream The Social Network on Pluto or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, still craving legal drama, tech-sector skulduggery, or more David-versus-Goliath courtroom fireworks? Here are a few more movies that fans of Cupertino will love.

It has been revealed that it’s set nowhere near Silicon Valley, but Michael Clayton is a real barn-burner of a paranoid legal thriller. George Clooney plays the title role, a “fixer” for a significant-money law firm. When his mentor and friend, Arthur Edens (Tom Wilkinson), suffers a mental breakdown while working on a case involving a toxic weedkiller produced by one of the firm’s clients and becomes a security threat, he’s assassinated, and Clayton is forced to reckon with his role in the world and how much injustice he’s willing to tolerate in exchange for money. It’s tense, smart, and has a wonderfully satisfying conclusion that fans of legal dramas where the good guys are willing to sacrifice (and win) will cheer. Rent Michael Clayton on Prime Video.

Based on real events, Dark Waters will appeal to anyone who likes to see smart lawyers take on enormous corporations in a search for the truth. A successful corporate lawyer, Robert Bilott (Mark Ruffalo), looks into a series of bizarre cattle deaths in rural West Virginia and stumbles onto evidence that the DuPont corporation has been dumping illegal, unregulated chemicals into the groundwater. Bilott’s years-long effort to hold DuPont responsible for the health impact on the community nearly costs him everything, but his determination to make the system work is ultimately the kind of inspiring legal story fans of Cupertino will appreciate. Rent Dark Waters on Prime Video.

If you just want the simple pleasures of a thrilling legal procedural, you can’t do much better than A Civil Action. John Travolta (at the height of his comeback) plays attorney Jan Schlichtmann, who takes on a class action lawsuit against two huge corporations because he thinks the case will be lucrative and relatively straightforward. As the case saps his resources and brings his firm to the brink of collapse, however, Schlichtmann slowly realizes that he’s fighting for more than just a substantial payday. Fair warning: This isn’t a feel-good movie in many ways, but it definitely brings those David-versus-Goliath vibes that Cupertino trades in. Rent A Civil Action on Prime Video.

Sources indicate that the true story behind the effort to license the video game Tetris from the Soviet-era Russian government doesn’t have the same stakes as many of the stories in Cupertino, and it’s certainly no longer timely. But the globe-trotting legal maze that Henk Rogers (Taron Egerton) must navigate to secure the rights, which seem to keep twisting and slipping from his grasp as various political and corporate interests weigh in, is just as fun and fascinating as the legal battles on the show. Tetris may no longer be a novel sensation in the gaming world, but it’s fascinating to see how something so baked into modern pop culture achieved that status. Stream Tetris on Apple TV or rent it on Prime Video.

If your favorite part of Cupertino is its exploration of the way tech companies impact our lives, and the way decisions made in obscure corporate offices can have enormous consequences, BlackBerry will be a favorite. Based on true events, it tells the story of how Research in Motion (RIM) created what was, for a time, the most dominant phone in the world—and how the company lost everything when its leaders took their eye off the ball and let personal obsessions and grudges impede their work. With a cast that includes Jay Baruchel and Glenn Howerton, this story of Silicon Valley hubris is right on target for Cupertino fans. Stream Blackberry on Netflix, Kanopy, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

Guns might be the weapon of choice for most Grand Theft Auto 6 players, but it turns out some enterprising digital criminals are taking a more inventive approach to robberies. Who needs a gun by their side when you've got a crate of beer?

Recent findings suggest that ordinarily, when you're attempting a store robbery in GTA 6, you first need to take out the guards - lethally or otherwise - before holding up the staff behind the till. But if you make too much of a commotion, the police show up and things turn sour. So players have been trying all sorts of tricks to avoid raising suspicion. And they've discovered an empty bottle can be thrown at the heads of staff and guards to put them out of action without making a lot of noise. It's non-lethal too!

A post shared by 1- UP Gaming (@1upgaming03).

In a video posted to Instagram, for instance, we see a player casually walking into a jewelry store with a crate of beer under one arm and a swift right hook ready to go in the other. That's when Jason goes on a throwing spree, knocking out staff with some well-placed projectiles to the head and dusting up those who get a little close. Aside from a very brief alarm from a locked door, the robbery goes smoothly.

A post shared by Kotov GTA6 стримы (@kotov.plays).

A faster, less flash example shows a quick and easy shop robbery where a casual bottle to the bloke behind the counter allows for rapid access to the cash in the till. Whether bottles can be utilised for something more complicated, like a full-on bank heist, remains to be seen.

Bottles, though, are just the tip of the iceberg. Roadkill and random lizards on the street also make for handy non-lethal projectiles. Beer remains the more compelling option, however. In gun terms, beer crates have up to six rounds in their 'magazine', making them a reliable single source of stuff to throw at folks.

Current cast member Mikey Day was joined by his OG co-stars Tom Hanks and Bobby Moynihan for what hilariously turned out to be several minutes of freezing in place while James Austin Johnson paused the sketch for his President Trump impression. The bit went over very well with fans at home, but it turns out the broadcast version contained a key change suggested by Tom Hanks who was looking out for everyone’s bodies.

During the original version, Hanks, Moynihan and Day all apparently froze in really exaggerated and over the top poses. Unfortunately for them, they didn’t realize that Johnson’s part with Trump was going to go on for so long. He ultimately talked for four minutes, which left the Pumpkins trio gassed by the time they had to unfreeze and act again. So, Hanks suggested they make a change before the live show.

Here’s how Moynihan described the conversation he had with Hanks after dress rehearsal to Mashable….

Sources indicate that in between dress and air, Tom came over to me and was like, ‘Hey, so, we’re all going to close our mouths.’ We were all doing our poses for dress, and on air, we’re just (standing there with our arms folded). We knew we had to stand there for the whole sketch. Tom Hanks is a good actor. He knew (we should) keep our mouths shut, keep our arms down. You don’t want to hold them up for the whole seven minutes of the cold open.

Recent findings suggest that moynihan said they probably would have figured all of this out before dress rehearsal, but they actually weren't paying much attention to the larger sketch. Instead, they spent like an hour talking about how absolutely absurd they felt being back in the costumes David S Pumpkins and the Skeletons, who have their own wild names. None of them ever thought the original sketch was going to hit, let alone lead to a TV special and an anniversary sketch a decade later.

You can watch the sketch in its entirety below….

Sources indicate that that’s the power of SNL though. Some of the sketches that go viral and live on in people’s memories involve sharp political commentary or really thoughtful parodies of society. Others just involve a goofy character or characters that connect with people for whatever reason. David S Pumpkins and the Skeletons are definitely examples of those characters. They’re just so over the top and ridiculous that you can’t look away, even if they’re frozen in the background of a President Trump sketch and trying to stay as still as possible.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a major bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to new estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.
  • Industry observers note that writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active users (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 rolled out on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million.
  • In a recent development, "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a major bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to new estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.

Industry observers note that writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active users (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 rolled out on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million. On PlayStation, which Elliott describes as "CoD's main platform", the drop was 44 percent.

In a recent development, "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote. "It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

Fortnite and FC 27 took a hit too, but both are already recovering. Fortnite's DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox fell 28 percent, from 17.8 million to 12.8 million, but by the end of the weekend it had clawed its way back to 19 percent below its baseline.

Epic is also holding a live event to close out the current season on 5th December, which Elliott says the studio "hopes will pull players back after they’ve polished off GTA 6’s story".

FC 27's DAUs dropped by around 27 percent, from 5.9 million to 4.3 million, and it's already back within 20 percent of its baseline.

GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD (@alineaanalytics estimates).COD HQ's daily active users across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M. On PlayStation – CoD’s main platform – Call of Duty took a 44% hit. Sadly, CoD has barely bounced… pic.twitter.com/XLa6N9TBfr.

According to Alinea, of those who'd played GTA 6 by the end of its launch weekend, 29 percent had also played Fortnite this month, 16 percent had played Call of Duty HQ, and 11 percent had played FC 27.

Elliott mentioned the pattern is largely what Alinea had predicted: the big live service games took an instant hit from GTA, but bounced back "because they're ingrained habits". Call of Duty is "the outlier here", he added, "and Xbox should - candidly - be worried about one of its premier franchises".

Sources indicate that elliott also points out that all of this is the impact of GTA 6's single-player mode. He expects its online component and PC port to arrive "some time next year", and when they do, he states, "the bounce back will not be so obtainable".

Alinea also estimates that GTA 6 has sold 44.9 million copies and made more than $4 billion since launch.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. While it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

According to recent reports, eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We’ve all experienced gift panic—that sinking feeling when you realize you need a present in an hour and you just don’t have one to give. Whether you spent all year chasing the “perfect” gift or simply procrastinated, your time is nearly up. But don’t panic. The clock may have nearly run out, but your options haven’t. Before you resort to re-gifting something from the back of a closet, here’s how to pull off a last-minute gift that is effortless but feels elevated and worthy of the person you’re giving it to.

It has been revealed that with the right presentation, even the most last-minute gift can read as thoughtful. Any performer will tell you that the difference between a good show and a bad one comes down to commitment and confidence. The same is true for last-minute gifts: If you act like your gift is thoughtful and intentional, they’ll think it is. The biggest mistake people make is apologizing as they hand over a present—nothing ruins a vibe faster than, “Sorry this is so last-minute.” So give with confidence.

Recent findings suggest that and focus on presentation. A handwritten note that contains a shared memory or personal joke can elevate a present. Use simple but personal wrapping; craft paper and twine, or a reusable gift bag that looks like you planned ahead. Add a small flourish, like a sprig of holly or a fancy bow. Small touches can make it seem like you’ve carefully prepared. What you don’t want are obvious panic gifts that scream, “I grabbed this on the way here.” The goal is effortless, not frantic.

In a recent development, digital gifts are your friends. You can order something in minutes that arrives instantly online, and with a little thought, will still read as personal and intentional. The trick is choosing a present that speaks to the recipient’s tastes, hobbies, or quirks, and pairing it with a small note to show you remember what they love. From e-books to streaming subscriptions, these gifts hit the sweet spot of thoughtful and last-minute. Here are some suggestion:.

When time is running out, gift cards are your secret weapon. They arrive instantly online, don’t require shipping, and with the right presentation, they can feel surprisingly thoughtful. The key is to pick a card that fits the recipient’s interests and add a personal note. The more specific you are, the better. If your giftee is into Italian food, get them an Eataly gift card. If they're a PC gamer, get them a Steam card. If they're into education, a membership to Skillshare is perfect. There's a gift card out there for just about any interest, and all you have to do it google it and email it.

Generic gift cards can be a last-minute lifesaver that can still seem a little personal if you give them the right way.

Recent findings suggest that pick a theme or design: Many online cards, like Amazon, Etsy, or Starbucks, let you choose designs. The right visual makes the card feel more intentional.

Include a warm, personal message: Even one line can make a digital card feel thoughtful—something like, “I couldn’t pick just one thing for you. Hope this helps you treat yourself.”.

Send strategically: Deliver the card by email or text, but consider printing the email or screenshotting it in a small envelope so it feels like a “real” gift.

Sign someone up for a subscription service, write a note explaining you want to keep giving them presents all year, and you're golden. Here are some suggestions:.

SnackCrate: This service sends a different snack from around the world every month.

According to recent reports, spiceClub: For the culinary adventurer on your list. A subscription to RawSpiceBar’s Spice Club delivers a curated selection of spices every month.

Recent findings suggest that mocktail Club: Booze-free fancy drinks delivered once a month? Sign me up.

Thera Box: If you know someone in need of some self-care, this once-a-month box is packed with wellness and relaxation items.

Loot Crate: If your giftee is geeky, consider this monthly surprise box of pop culture treasures.

Recent findings suggest that cameo is a platform where celebrities, influencers, musicians, and performers create personalized video messages for fans. If someone on your list is a fan of someone on Cameo, you can set up a session, and give a card with a mysterious note like "Keep an eye out for a special message." They'll be delighted with a personal message from wrestling legend Mick Foley or terrified when Chris Hansen appears on their screen; your choice.

I have enough crap in my house, so I love getting experiences instead of things. The challenge with experience gifts is usually timing: Many require reservations or coordination, but there are plenty of options that let your giftee schedule the time, making them perfect last-minute gifts.

Museum membership cards: Many institutions sell digital gift memberships that the recipient can activate whenever they like.

Movie tickets: Your local multiplex probably has a gift certificate you can buy online.

Local attraction passes: Some city attractions offer gift cards or “anytime admission” tickets that don’t expire immediately.

Pair these with a note explaining why you chose the experience, or, if you have that kind of relationship, something like, "I want to take you to the Museum of Modern Art." Just make sure you follow through and actually go.

It has been revealed that sometimes, there’s literally no time to order, wrap, or even think about a gift. If you’re scrambling out the door and need something now, you might be able to fake your way through, even if you're stopping at the liquor store on the way to the Christmas party.

In a recent development, flowers or a small potted plant: Give a seasonal bouquet or a small indoor plant. Add a handwritten note, even a single line, and it might come off as thoughtful.

Gourmet chocolates or candy: Specialty chocolates from a local shop or grocery store display can feel luxe with a little ribbon or bag.

Wine, craft beer, or non-alcoholic beverage: A bottle with a clean label or interesting packaging immediately elevates your gift. Ask the clerk at the liquor store to help you find something unique.

Lottery tickets: Who wouldn't appreciate a bunch of scratch-off lottery tickets?

Hard cash is the most impersonal gift of all, but the only one you know will be used. This gift really depends on the person getting it, so be aware of whether they're likely to think "Just what I wanted!" or "Wait, I'm not poor." If you give cash, make sure it's crisp bills in a nice card, with a personalized note.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, how dare you accuse me of being a friendless loser!
  • With friends like these, who needs human allies?
  • Let's try that again: wireheady heist-me-do Cyber Knights: Flashpoint has received a major revision adding a fresh player class, the Drone Pilot, billed by developers Trese Brothers as "the most complex" and among the most "flexible" of the game's Neuromantic vocations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, how dare you accuse me of being a friendless loser! I have loads of friends! Their names are R2-D2 and Clippy and Arnold and Rosie the Maid. They all live in my rucksack, ready and waiting should I need somebody to dupe a security guard or fill the air around me with explosive chaff. All except Clippy, that is. He's too chonky to stuff in a bag, which can make for tricky mission extractions, but he compensates for that with his generous selection of *voice drops six octaves* FULLY LOADED AUTOCANNONS.

With friends like these, who needs human allies? It's time to play stealth tactics sim Cyber Knights: Flashpoint the way it was meant to be played: skulking in a hole while buzzing, clanking mechabastards cleanse the map of any and all defenders. Don't spare the lead, Rosie. You were not built to understand mercy.

Let's try that again: wireheady heist-me-do Cyber Knights: Flashpoint has received a major revision adding a fresh player class, the Drone Pilot, billed by developers Trese Brothers as "the most complex" and among the most "flexible" of the game's Neuromantic vocations. The Drone Pilot arrives alongside a new pet system they'll be using down the road for "warhunds and assassin cats". Right now, though, the only "pets" at your disposal appear to be those drones. Here's what they're good for: "jamming enemy systems, disabling security devices in passing, hijacking enemy drones to turn on their own side, or trailing fields of shredding nano-chaff and squad-boosting support zones wherever the drone flies.".

Recent findings suggest that drones come in three types, light (fast and best for stealthy support), medium (a mix of support and combat-oriented), and heavy (flying forts and/or stomping murder mechs). Light or medium drones are deployed from your backpack, and auto-extract when you do, no matter where they are. Heavy drones deploy alongside you at mission start, and have to be within nine metres of you when you extract, potentially trapping you on the map. Each drone chassis has its own weapon and armour setup, plus a choice of modules that grant Talents (abilities).

While rolling a Drone Pilot might seem like an opportunity to forgo any and all squidgy organic accomplices, the major catch is that Drone Pilots and their mecha mates share action and movement points. While using the Full Pilot talent, you can transfer AP to a drone so that it can move and fight like a full separate character. While using the Auto-Pilot talent, you'll only share bonus MP. There's also the option to multi-class, with Trese Brothers noting that "dipping into another class can significantly increase their flexibility or buff their personal abilities with just a few talents from an alternate tree".

As for how you'll get your hands on the Drone Pilot class, their costs make them a poor fit for teams with a power level below three, so they aren't among the New Game options. You'll be able to recruit them in the Underworld Hub and also, turn characters into drone pilots once you acquire a Pilot Wire cybernetic implant and the requisite cyber surgery. The Pilot Wire uses up a Deep Brain slot, making the class incompatible with the Hacker or Wireghost classes. Beyond that, you can reach out to a smuggler or broker to get access to new and better drones and pilot cybernetics.

Pettable killdroids aside, Trese Brothers are continuing work on Cyber Knight's mod support. The latest enhancement adds features for official language translation mods and Attribute bonus tweaking, alongside expanded Legwork options. They're also labouring away on a modkit preview project of some kind. Read more on Steam.

Industry observers note that newly introduced to Cyber Knights? Congratulations on digesting all the above gibberish about weaponised WALL-Es. I can only assume you read the whole thing in hopes of further talk of "assassin cats", but alas, Trese Brothers are maintaining an ominous silence. Instead, here is what Nic Reuben (RPS in peace) had to say about the game in our 2025 review: "Don't let its initial cyber-posturing and sheer amount of systems intimidate you. Cyber Knights: Flashpoint is wider than it is oppressively deep, while still being rich enough to offer up some excellently tense and entertaining stealth tactics.".

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

CD Projekt Red has noted people can expect a similar qualitative and technological leap from The Witcher 3 to The Witcher 4 as has been witnessed between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6.

CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski made the remark during a Q3 earnings call this afternoon, during which he and CDPR faced a handful of questions related to GTA 6.

"First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," Nowakowski began by saying, "but I do understand the connection here. Having noted that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game, we did see the differences.

Sources indicate that "We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 - I think so, yes. It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4.".

Another question was about whether GTA 6 had affected development prepares for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 - a question well-timed after Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski joked at the weekend that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled" because of how impressive GTA 6 is.

According to recent reports, "Is seeing GTA 6 launch making us make the games more expensive?" said Nowakowski. "We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [4] and Cyberpunk 2; they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's [that it's] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers.".

Specifically in terms of budget, Nowakowski said nothing had changed, and also echoed a point made earlier this year when he said Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 are "not budget-driven developments".

Industry observers note that "I'm not saying we don't care about the budgets: we do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well. But you cannot make games like that having in mind 'this is the fixed number of money I want to spend and that's it, otherwise I'm gone'," he noted.

Industry observers note that "They're ambition-driven developments and money's key - the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is like I noted, and honestly that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release; it has just always been like that.".

Recent findings suggest that when asked whether the arrival of GTA 6 had impacted sales of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, Nowakowski answered "yes and no". "You do see a certain dip in engagement on the PlayStation and Xbox for sure," he remarked.

Statistics apparently show a drop of "at least" 25 percent in CDPR's players as they "engaged themselves with GTA 6". "But you do have to remember that a lot of our players are PC-based," Nowakowski pointed out. "GTA has not debuted on PC; we have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales or engagement. So it's a bit of a mixed answer.

According to recent reports, "And also on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero," he added. "Some short impact, yes, on the consoles. Long-term, we do not really see that affecting ourselves in any material way in Q4.".

Finally, the questioning turned to marketing, which Rockstar has shown can reach far and wide if you have the brand-power of GTA and some imagination. We've seen prestigious department stores like Selfridges taken over by Rockstar for GTA 6, trailers premiering on Netflix, Miami launch festivals - Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

CDPR is no stranger to grabbing headlines with glitzy actor hirings such as Keanu Reeves, but will Rockstar's approach to marketing GTA 6 push it a step further?

It has been revealed that "The most key takeaway - I'm not sure if I'd call it a lesson because this is our playbook as well - is that if you want to reach a certain critical mass, you do have to get out of just the core gaming bubble, something we did in the past as well," Nowakowski stated. "For sure, GTA 6 went there.

According to recent reports, "If the underlying question was if we're going to repeat or copy-paste their playbook: no, for sure not. Our games are different and they require a certain different approach - we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: this is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future.".

Industry observers note that CDPR's Q3 financial results were positive. The tech giant made less money than this time last year, but the "fresh momentum" - as Nowakowski put it - provided to The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 by the release of the Remastered edition of Witcher 3 and the Edgerunners anime series on Netflix, and associated game update, went a long way.

Industry observers note that the Witcher 3 reached its highest concurrent player count on Steam as a result, and Cyberpunk 2077 reached its second highest concurrent player count, which represents serious staying power for both games so long after they were first released. And with Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past on track for 2027, and The Witcher 4 for 2028, the future is loaded.
